description: Line-ending policy for the three-OS suite (repair after the 0.verifyh GATE-FAILED, ci.yml run 34037147355: ubuntu and macos 431/431 green, windows-latest 99 of 419 failed in 6 files, every failure `\r\n` versus `\n`; cause: `.gitattributes` had no text/eol policy, so `actions/checkout@v4` on Windows converted every LF file to CRLF at checkout, and six tests read fixtures/markdown/**, packages/core/test/fixtures/** and docs/MARKDOWN-STYLE.md byte-for-byte; DECISIONS #018). Replace the whole of `.gitattributes` with exactly these four lines, in this order, nothing more: `* text=auto eol=lf` / `fixtures/** -text` / `packages/core/test/fixtures/** -text` / `docs/lessons.md merge=union` (each on its own line, one trailing newline). The `-text` trees are read byte-for-byte by tests and stay verbatim on every OS (fixtures/markdown/crlf-line-endings.md is the corpus's one CRLF source by design); everything else is LF on every checkout, which is what docs/MARKDOWN-STYLE.md needs and what the next byte-for-byte reader will need. Scope is that one file plus the journal and lessons: no test edits, no workflow edits, no source edits, zero new dependencies (PRD §4). Do not widen or narrow the attribute lines; do not run `git config core.autocrlf` (repo config is shared by every worktree) — use `git -c core.autocrlf=true <cmd>` for the one-command simulation in the acceptance.
acceptance: `cat .gitattributes` is byte-identical to the four lines in the description. Reproduction first, recorded in the journal: before the change, `rm -r docs/MARKDOWN-STYLE.md fixtures/markdown packages/core/test/fixtures && git -c core.autocrlf=true checkout -- docs/MARKDOWN-STYLE.md fixtures packages/core/test/fixtures` (a Windows-style checkout) followed by `git ls-files --eol docs/MARKDOWN-STYLE.md fixtures packages/core/test/fixtures | grep -c 'w/crlf'` reports more than one path, and `pnpm test` is red. After the change, the same two commands report `w/crlf` for exactly one path, fixtures/markdown/crlf-line-endings.md (`i/crlf`, `attr/-text`), `git ls-files --eol | grep 'i/crlf'` still lists only that path (no renormalisation of tracked content), and `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` is green on that Windows-style checkout. `git diff --stat` against the branch base touches only `.gitattributes`, `docs/lessons.md` and `docs/progress/journal-main.md`. Honest statement: this container is Linux, so the in-container result is a proxy and not a Windows pass; the only proof is the `0.verify.g1h` gate green on ubuntu, macos and windows, which this task cannot observe and must not claim.

description: Phase 0 review fix (DECISIONS #review-0-r0 F1, Claude findings 1–2 and Sol finding 2, blocker): packages/core/src/sentences.ts `sliceInline` gives a zero-width atomic inline node (an image with empty alt, `![](x.png)`, alone or inside a link) no owner at the end of a paragraph and two owners at offset 0, so `replaceSentence` and `reorderSentences` silently delete or duplicate it; the mark branch's `hi <= lo` test discards zero-width descendants the same way. Decide the ownership rule for width-0 inline nodes at slice endpoints once (an explicit `includeAtTo` argument, true only for the final slice that reaches `plain.length`; drop the `zeroWidth && start === from` special case), traverse wrappers (link, emphasis, strong) that contain them, write the rule in the doc comment, and add the invariant the corpus never had: for every top-level paragraph of every fixture listed in fixtures/markdown/index.json, `format(reorderSentences(root, id, identity))` and `format(replaceSentence(root, id, i, <the sentence's own text>))` equal `format(root)` byte-for-byte. No new dependencies; no edits outside packages/core/src/sentences.ts and packages/core/test/.
acceptance: Probe cases from the reports pass as tests, each asserting node presence, count and URL, presence and absence: `One. Two. ![](i.png)` with replaceSentence(index 0, 'X.') → `X. Two. ![](i.png)` and reorderSentences(identity) unchanged; `![](i.png) One. Two.` with replaceSentence(index 0, 'X.') → exactly one image; `Hi. ![](x.png)` identity reorder unchanged; a linked empty-alt image `[![](x.png)](https://e.x)` at the end and at the start survives replace and reorder with its URL; an image adjacent to another image survives. The corpus-wide identity invariant passes for every paragraph of every fixture in index.json (count read from the index, not written as a literal). The 30 cases of sentences.cases.json and the existing sentences tests still pass; `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` green.

description: Phase 0 review fix (DECISIONS #review-0-r0 F2, Sol findings 3 and 5, blocker): packages/core/src/sidecar.ts's hand-written front-matter scalar scanner treats malformed scalars as writable (`title: bad: mapping`, `title: "\q"`) and misdecodes valid double-quoted escapes (`"\u0041"` mirrored as `u0041`, not `A`); a replacement value containing a newline is written literally inside single quotes as two physical lines and reported as success. Define the supported grammar for the two app-owned keys (PRD §6.1): plain scalar with no `: ` or ` #` sequence and no leading indicator character; double-quoted with the YAML escapes `\\ \" \n \t \r \/ \b \f \0 \uXXXX \xXX` decoded and re-encoded; single-quoted with `''`. Everything else (unknown escapes, malformed plain scalars, block or flow indicators, a replacement value containing `\n` or `\r` for any quoting style) → `FrontMatterUnsupported` before any edit, root identity and every byte unchanged. No YAML library (PRD §4; zero new dependencies); edits only in packages/core/src/sidecar.ts and packages/core/test/.
acceptance: Tests assert, for each case, both the outcome and the untouched bytes: `"\u0041"` reads as `A` and re-encodes preserving the quoting; `"\q"` and `bad: mapping` reads report FrontMatterUnsupported and a write leaves the block byte-identical; a multiline replacement (`Line one\nLine two`, and with `\r`) is refused for plain, single-quoted and double-quoted titles; the existing sidecar tests (73 at r0) still pass; `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` green.

description: Phase 0 review fix (DECISIONS #review-0-r0 F3, Claude findings 3 and 10, Sol finding 10, Grok findings 5–6, should-fix required): the green bar `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` (CLAUDE.md step 2, RUNNER-SPEC §4.3) covers neither `tsc` nor coverage, so packages/core ships red on `pnpm --filter @essaydown/core typecheck` (packages/core/test/sidecar.test.ts:979, TS2339: `variants` on an un-narrowed `orphans[0].entry` union) and 0.7's 100% blocks.ts threshold is never executed. Widen the bar's existing commands, not its command list: root `package.json` `lint` becomes `eslint . && pnpm -r --if-present typecheck` (every package with a `typecheck` script runs `tsc --noEmit`; add the script to packages that lack it), `test` becomes `vitest run --coverage` (thresholds fail the run) with `coverage` kept for the table. Fix the narrowing at sidecar.test.ts:979 with a discriminant check (`list === 'rewrites'`) rather than a cast. Set global per-file thresholds in vitest.config.ts at or just below the values the current `pnpm coverage` run prints (read them from the run; do not copy numbers from this text), keeping blocks.ts at 100. ci.yml needs no change (it already runs `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test`). No new dependencies.
acceptance: `pnpm lint` fails on a deliberately introduced type error in a scratch file and passes once it is removed (both shown in the journal); `pnpm test` fails when blocks.ts's threshold is lowered below its measurement to a value that cannot be met and passes at the committed values (shown in the journal, then reverted); `pnpm --filter @essaydown/core typecheck` exits 0; `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` green; `git diff --stat` shows no dependency-manifest or lockfile change.

description: Phase 0 review fix (DECISIONS #review-0-r0 F4 and F5, Claude findings 4–5, Sol finding 8, Grok finding 1, should-fix required): (1) .github/workflows/ci.yml's `merge-logs` job merges the three per-OS `test-logs-<os>` artifacts with the default `separate-directories: false`, so `lint.log`/`test.log`/`cargo-test.log` collide and the accepted, digest-verified artifact holds one OS; set `separate-directories: true` (the merged artifact then holds `test-logs-{ubuntu,macos,windows}-latest/{lint,test,cargo-test}.log`); (2) the runner's conformance suite `ralph/test/run.sh` (RUNNER-SPEC §12) is run only by bootstrap: add a step to the ubuntu leg of the `test` job that runs `bash ralph/test/run.sh` after `cargo test`, its output captured as `ralph-test.log` inside that leg's upload. description: Phase 0 review fix (DECISIONS #review-0-r1 G1, G2, G7 and G8; Sol finding 2 and Claude finding 1, blocker; Grok finding 1 and Claude finding 3, should-fix required): packages/core/src/sidecar.ts's front-matter writer still disagrees with its reader about what is representable. (a) Key identity: `KEY_LINE` compares literal key spellings, so a double- or single-quoted spelling of an app-owned key is neither a duplicate of the plain spelling nor found on its own; `writeFrontMatter` then rewrites the plain line beside the quoted duplicate (ok:true, the duplicate stays), or appends a second spelling. Rule: any quoted spelling of `title` or `question` in the block makes that key unsupported (FrontMatterUnsupported, root identity, every byte unchanged) whether it appears alone or beside the plain spelling; the block's other keys stay readable. (b) One quoting predicate: `needsQuoting` tests only tab, newline, `#`, `:` and the leading indicator, and the single-quoted branch of `serializeScalar` escapes only the apostrophe, so a replacement value containing U+0000, another C0 or C1 control, DEL, U+2028, U+2029 or a lone surrogate is written raw with ok:true; invariant A then fails on the written document, and `KEY_LINE` (a dot under the u flag without the s flag) classifies the block as malformed on the next read. Derive every quoting decision from one predicate that owns `encodeDoubleQuoted`'s escape table (plus U+2028, U+2029 and lone surrogates), route the single-quoted branch through it (promote to double-quoted rather than emit raw), and match key lines with an explicit character class instead of a dot. (c) The unchanged-value skip runs after the newline refusal, so a no-op write of a double-quoted value whose decoded form contains a newline (which the reader accepted and classified writable) is refused: run the `entry.value === value` skip first and refuse only a value that would actually be rewritten. (d) The rule promoted into CLAUDE.md names an unchanged front-matter value as a corpus-wide identity case and no test carries it. No YAML library, no new dependencies; edits only in packages/core/src/sidecar.ts and packages/core/test/.
acceptance: Tests assert both the outcome and the untouched bytes for: a quoted duplicate of `question` beside the plain spelling returns FrontMatterUnsupported with `write.root === root` and the block byte-identical (double-quoted, single-quoted and escaped spellings, alone and paired with the plain one); values containing U+0000, U+0007, U+007F, U+0085, U+2028, U+2029 and a lone surrogate either round-trip through a double-quoted scalar with invariant A holding on the written document or are refused before any edit, never written raw; the inverse property readable(v) === !needsQuoting(v) holds over a value table that includes those code points and the four printable strings the existing test uses; a no-op write of a double-quoted value with a decoded newline returns ok:true with `changed` empty and `write.root === root`; a corpus-wide test over every fixture in fixtures/markdown/index.json that carries a yaml node writes each writable app-owned key back with the value just read and asserts `format` output is byte-identical, and asserts a non-writable key returns FrontMatterUnsupported with root identity (fixture names read from the index, never a literal count); the existing sidecar and front-matter-grammar tests still pass; `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` green.

description: Phase 0 review fix (DECISIONS #review-0-r1 G3, Sol finding 3, should-fix required): packages/core/src/sentences.ts rebuilds slices for an identity permutation and for a sentence replaced by its own Markdown, so an inline mark spanning a sentence boundary is split: `**First sentence. Second sentence.**` reordered by [0, 1] becomes `**First sentence.** **Second sentence.**`, and a link spanning two sentences becomes two links with the intervening space moved out of the link. The corpus-wide identity invariant of 0.14 did not catch it because no indexed fixture carries a strong, emphasis, link or delete mark across a sentence boundary. Do three things: (1) after input validation, an identity permutation and a replacement whose Markdown equals the sentence's own (`sentenceMarkdown`) return a tree that formats byte-identically (short-circuit on the validated no-op, not on a string comparison of the output); (2) add LF fixtures under fixtures/markdown with canonical siblings and index.json entries, at least one paragraph each with strong, emphasis, a link and strikethrough spanning a sentence boundary, plus one with a mark spanning the first boundary and one the last, so invariants A/B/C and the 0.14 identity invariant cover them (counts are read from the index and the directory; tests that read the directory keep working); (3) state in the doc comment the rule for a real replacement or reorder under a spanning mark (which sentence keeps the mark and what happens at the boundary) and test it at the first, middle and last position, choosing the rule that leaves the bytes of every untouched sentence unchanged. No new dependencies; edits only in packages/core/src/sentences.ts, packages/core/test/ and fixtures/markdown/.
acceptance: Sol's two probes pass as tests: the identity reorder of `**First sentence. Second sentence.**` and the self-replacement of the first sentence of `[First sentence. Second sentence.](https://example.com)` both format byte-identically to the input; the new fixtures appear in fixtures/markdown/index.json with canonical siblings and pass invariants A/B/C and the corpus-wide identity invariant (the roundtrip matrix grows by three per fixture, count read from the index, not a literal); the spanning-mark rule for real edits is tested at the first, middle and last positions with the untouched sentence's bytes asserted unchanged; the 30 cases of sentences.cases.json and the existing sentences and zero-width tests still pass; `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` green.

description: Phase 0 review fix (DECISIONS #review-0-r1 G4 and G5, Sol finding 1 and Claude finding 6, should-fix required; runner code, conformance tests required): (1) `ralph/lib/util.mjs` `breakStaleLock` renames a lock it judged stale before it compares bytes, so between the rename and the compare the lock path is free: with A holding a live lock, a breaker B that read the crashed holder's bytes earlier renames A's lock away, a third entrant C creates the path and runs its critical section beside A, and B's compare fails too late (Sol's probe, `/logs/reviews/0/r1/sol/lock-probe.mjs` and `lock-probe.log`: third entrant inside the critical section while the live holder is active). Cut automatic stale-lock breaking to a manual procedure, as CLAUDE.md prefers: `withLock` never renames or unlinks a lock it did not create; a lock whose pid is dead makes `withLock` throw a `RalphError` naming the file, the dead pid and the manual recovery (confirm with `pgrep` that no `ralph.sh`, `gate.sh` or admin process exists, then remove `.locks/ralph` by hand), and `ralph.sh doctor` reports `stale-lock <pid>` with that same repair (a read-only check in 0.19's pattern). Delete `breakStaleLock` and the `hooks.beforeBreak` interleaving point; keep the token re-read after acquisition and the token-scoped release; rewrite the doc comment. (2) `writeAtomic` swallows a failed directory fsync in a bare catch, so a close intent written without directory durability leaves no trace: on that failure append one line (`writeAtomic: directory fsync failed <path> <code>`) to the audit log the state layer already writes, before continuing. Conformance tests: a stale lock (dead pid) makes `withLock` refuse with the recovery message and nothing under state/ changes; Sol's three-actor interleaving, reproduced with the fs hooks the suite already owns, shows the live holder's path is never freed and the third entrant waits until timeout; `doctor` lists `stale-lock` and is clean after the manual removal; the injected-fs `writeAtomic` test records the audit line when the directory open or fsync throws. docs/RUNNER-SPEC.md §1 already says stale locks are manual (this reconciliation); do not edit it. No new dependencies; the diff touches only ralph/lib/util.mjs, ralph/lib/doctor.mjs, ralph/test/ and the journal.
acceptance: `bash ralph/test/run.sh` green with the new tests failing before the fix (the journal shows the red run); the identifier `breakStaleLock` no longer appears under ralph/lib/; the existing lock and writeAtomic tests still pass or are rewritten to the new contract with the reason in the journal; `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` green.

description: macOS keymap tests exercise the platform route (repair after the 1.verifyh GATE-FAILED, ci.yml run 34333160626 at 3e98707: ubuntu-latest and windows-latest green on every test file, macos-latest 2 test files and 5 tests failed — `packages/editor/test/store.test.ts` › `undoKeymap (rendered view)` › "undoes on Ctrl+z", "redoes on the shifted-letter route, where the event's key is 'Z'", "redoes on the keyCode route, where the event's key is not a letter", "is installed by storePlugins, ahead of the editing keymaps", and `packages/editor/test/toggle.test.ts` › `the chord` › "Cmd/Ctrl+/ reaches a ProseMirror keymap" — each `expected false to be true` on the handled boolean; the log is /logs/ci/1.verifyh/a1/workflow.log; DECISIONS #020). Fix the tests, not the chord. Inject the platform instead of reading the host's: stub `navigator` before the keymap library is imported (the constant is read at import, so this needs module isolation — `vi.stubGlobal` + `vi.resetModules()` + a dynamic import of `prosemirror-keymap` and of the module under test inside the test, or an equivalent the task shows working in the reproduction); never a literal platform list copied from one run. For each of the four chords (`Mod-z`, `Mod-Z`, `Shift-Mod-z`, `Mod-/`) exercise both routes with presence and absence: on a Mac platform a `metaKey` event is handled and a `ctrlKey` event is not; on a non-Mac platform a `ctrlKey` event is handled and a `metaKey` event is not; the `storePlugins` ordering test follows the same rule. One test per guard, enumerated from the diff, and the journal names the test that discharges each guard. No `.skip`, `.only`, `runIf` or `skipIf` — nothing that leaves a route untested on any OS. description: Playwright in CI (repair after the 1.verifyh GATE-FAILED; handoff 009 Finding 4, DECISIONS #019 and #020): `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (task 0.2) runs `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` and `cargo test` and uploads `test-logs`, but installs no Playwright browser, never runs `e2e/web/` and uploads no `playwright-report`, so `1.verify`'s ciAcceptance ("Full suite + e2e/web (Playwright) green on all three runners") could never be met — run 34333160626 records `artifacts: []`, and the gate would have failed on the missing artifact had the macOS unit tests not failed first. Edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml` only. After the `Cargo test` step, on all three runners: (1) install the Playwright browser per OS at the version the lockfile pins — `pnpm --filter @essaydown/e2e-web exec playwright install --with-deps chromium` on Linux, the same without `--with-deps` on macOS and Windows (the browser cache is per runner; never assume it is present; the CLI lives only in e2e/web/node_modules/.bin, which the `--filter … exec` spelling reaches); (2) run every spec file under `e2e/web/` with `pnpm --filter @essaydown/e2e-web exec playwright test`, which starts the Vite `webServer` of e2e/web/playwright.config.ts (`pnpm --filter @essaydown/desktop dev`, `cwd` repo root, port 1420), with the HTML reporter writing e2e/web/playwright-report/ on every outcome and never opening a browser (`PLAYWRIGHT_HTML_OPEN=never` and `--reporter=list,html`, or the equivalent), so that any failing spec fails the step and the job — the failure lives in the job, `ciGate` refuses on `conclusion !== success`, and no artifact-content guard is built; (3) upload `playwright-report-${{ matrix.os }}` with `if: always()`, and in the existing `merge-logs` job merge the three into one artifact named exactly `playwright-report` (a second `actions/upload-artifact/merge@v4` step, `pattern: playwright-report-*`, `separate-directories: true`, `delete-merged: true`), so the report exists on failure too. The report is evidence for the 1.10 reviewers, never the pass condition. Keep the workflow on `push` to `ci/**` only; tool versions stay read from docker/versions.env; `shell: bash` on every new step like the rest of the file; no other step changes. No change to e2e/web/playwright.config.ts unless the reporter cannot be set from the workflow (then the smallest config change, stated in the journal); no manifest or lockfile change; zero new dependencies (PRD §4). Windows: the Vite dev server and the `pnpm --filter` spellings have never run there; the journal states that the Windows job log in /logs/ci/1.verify.g1h/a1/workflow.log is the first thing to read if the gate fails.

description:
Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r0 F2 — Sol finding 1 required): the ProseMirror schema in packages/editor/src/schema.ts defines `toDOM` for every node and mark and no `parseDOM` rule (the comment near line 94 says the native clipboard path is unused; it is not), so the editor's own copy → paste in the rendered view reconstructs the pasted HTML as plain text: `# Heading

**bold**
` selected, copied and pasted over itself becomes `Heading

bold
` (Sol's `/report/paste.cjs`, reproduced in docs/reviews/phase-1-r0-sol.md). Add `parseDOM` rules paired one-to-one with each `toDOM` — headings by level, paragraph, emphasis, strong, delete/strikethrough, link (href, title), image (src, alt, title), inline code, code block (language), blockquote, ordered list (start) and bullet list, list item, table/row/cell (alignment), thematic break, hard break — preserving every attribute the schema carries; the opaque `raw` atom round-trips by its stored value (a `data-` attribute or equivalent on its `toDOM`, read back by its rule) and its displayed text is never re-parsed as markup, so a pasted raw node cannot become executable HTML. Unit: a test that enumerates `schema.nodes` and `schema.marks` and asserts every one with a `toDOM` has a `parseDOM`, so a future node cannot be added without its rule; if a DOM is available in vitest without a new dependency, the corpus leg `DOMSerializer` → `DOMParser` → `eq` over every fixture in index.json, else the journal says so and the Playwright corpus leg below carries it. Playwright on /dev/editor: for every fixture in fixtures/markdown/index.json (loaded through the dev bar, count from the index), select all, copy, paste over the selection, and assert the markdown pane is byte-identical before and after; plus explicit cases for a heading, strong/emphasis, a nested list, a table, a fenced code block and a raw HTML block, and one case pasting plain text from the clipboard (set with the Playwright clipboard API) into a paragraph that stays plain. Scope: packages/editor/src/schema.ts, packages/editor/test/**, e2e/web/**, docs/lessons.md, the journal. Zero new dependencies (PRD §4).
acceptance: The enumeration test is present and green; the Playwright self copy/paste corpus leg is green for every fixture in index.json and byte-identical before and after (count from the index, never a literal); the six explicit structure cases and the plain-text case are green; the raw-node case asserts the pasted document contains the same `raw` node value and that no element from its text was created in the DOM; the existing 1.1 schema round-trip suite is unchanged and green; `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` green; `git diff --stat` against the branch base touches only packages/editor/src/schema.ts, packages/editor/test/**, e2e/web/**, docs/lessons.md and docs/progress/journal-main.md; no manifest or lockfile change.

description:
Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r0 F3 — Sol finding 4 required): `formatWithMap` in packages/core/src/positions.ts derives the ranges of nodes the serializer does not dispatch (table rows and cells) from their descendants' spans, so an empty cell or a wholly empty row has no range, and `nodeAt`/the map cannot resolve paths `0.1`, `0.1.0`, `0.1.1` of `| a | b |
| - | - |
| | |
` — the shape the 1.3 table input rule itself creates (`packages/editor/src/input.ts:179`), so a cursor toggle from the new empty body row has no mapping. Give every row and cell an explicit range from the table layout the serializer writes (delimiter positions), so an empty cell maps to its zero-width point between its delimiters; state the ownership rule for the zero-width cell once in the doc comment (CLAUDE.md's half-open-slice rule) and test the first, middle and last empty cells, a wholly empty body row, a table whose header cells are empty, and the cursor toggle from the newly created empty body row on /dev/editor (Playwright). Add one LF fixture with empty cells to fixtures/markdown/ with its index.json entry (paragraphStartLines and nodeTypes filled the way 0.22 did), so the positions-corpus test's "every node has a range" assertion covers cells with no descendants; the map stays pure (no DOM). Scope: packages/core/src/positions.ts, packages/core/test/**, fixtures/markdown/**, e2e/web/**, docs/lessons.md, the journal. Zero new dependencies (PRD §4).

Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r0 F4 — Sol findings 2 and 3 required; one class: source ↔ rendered cursor coordinates): (a) `apps/desktop/src/dev/DevEditor.tsx:92` passes the raw CodeMirror (line, ch) to the cursor map built from the canonical serialization, so a source edit that changes the canonical line layout moves the next rendered edit — `alpha



beta` with the cursor before `beta`, toggle, type `X` gives `alpha

betaX
`, expected `alpha

Xbeta
`; (b) `packages/editor/src/toggle.ts:233` maps character offsets ignoring escapes and continuation prefixes, so even canonical source lands the cursor on the wrong character — in `a\*b c` the PM position before `b` maps to source ch 2 (before `*`) instead of ch 3; in `> alpha
> beta gamma` the position before `beta` maps to line 2 ch 0 instead of ch 2. Fix: translate the live source cursor through the parsed node and its offset within that node into canonical coordinates before consulting the map (parse the live buffer and map through its own node/offset), and carry the serializer's per-character transformations (escapes, continuation prefixes, marker widths, indentation) in both directions, rather than assuming one source character per text character — if the formatter must export an offset table for this, add it to packages/core/src/positions.ts as a pure function and say so in the journal. Tests assert independently derived locations (Sol's lesson: a round trip through two mutually wrong functions, or an in-bounds check, proves nothing): extra blank lines, a Setext heading (`Alpha
=====`) and a `* item` list spelling, an escaped character, a blockquote prefix, a nested-list prefix, an emphasis marker, each with the expected (line, ch) and PM position written by hand from the canonical text; the translation creates no undo entry (the existing toggle/undo test stays green). Playwright: Sol's two reproductions as specs, asserting the exact markdown pane after the typed `X`. Scope: packages/editor/src/toggle.ts, apps/desktop/src/dev/DevEditor.tsx, packages/editor/test/**, e2e/web/**, packages/core/src/positions.ts and packages/core/test/** only for the exported offset table, docs/lessons.md, the journal. description: Phase 1 follow-up required by task 1.10's phase check ("typing latency p95 with 10k words on /dev/editor: < 16 ms or a follow-up task is inserted at reconciliation"; DECISIONS #review-1-r0 F5 — Claude findings 2 and 7, Sol finding 5 required). Measurements at r0, all Linux headless Chromium, Vite dev build: rendered view p95 15.0 / 13.9 / 14.1 ms at 10k words and 26.3 ms at 20k (Claude: keydown → first mutation of the markdown pane, both timestamps in-page, 120 presses); 38.6 / 39.5 ms (Sol: beforeinput → the next timer task after input and observer work); source view p95 40.6 ms at 10k words (Claude, same harness as its rendered run). The two protocols differ by 2.5× on the same tree, so the number is protocol-bound; the cost is not: every rendered doc-changing transaction runs `pmToMdast` over the whole document (`packages/editor/src/store.ts:167`), the /dev/editor snapshot re-runs `format(root)` on every `useSyncExternalStore` read (`apps/desktop/src/dev/DevEditor.tsx:72`), and every source-view keystroke re-parses the whole buffer (`packages/editor/src/toggle.ts:479`; `parse` is 37 ms at 10k words against `format` 0.9 ms). Three changes. (1) Cache the formatted snapshot by root identity so a read whose root is unchanged returns the same string instance without serialising. (2) Commit the source buffer on the coalescing boundary, not per update: schedule `parse` + commit on the `SOURCE_KEY` burst window (or an idle callback bounded by it), the CodeMirror buffer staying authoritative for what the user sees in between, the binding's `shownText` echo guard unchanged, undo grouping unchanged, and a toggle or an unmount flushing the pending commit first so nothing typed is lost (a test for the flush). (3) One Playwright spec, e2e/web/latency.spec.ts, whose doc comment states the protocol: a document generated in-test at 1k and 10k words of agent-written prose (never a personal text), the caret in a mid-document paragraph, N single-character presses after W warm-ups, latency = keydown timestamp to the first mutation of the markdown pane, both in-page; p50/p95 printed to the test output and attached as Playwright annotations, for the rendered view and for the source view. The assertion is a relationship, never a magnitude from one run (CLAUDE.md): p95 at 10k words is within a stated factor of p95 at 1k words, the factor and its reason in the spec's doc comment; the absolute numbers are evidence for the 1.10.r1 reviewers, who judge the 16 ms criterion from them under this protocol — never a CI pass condition on shared runners. Incremental `pmToMdast` is not built here: append the option with the r0 numbers to docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md. Scope: packages/editor/src/store.ts, packages/editor/src/toggle.ts, apps/desktop/src/dev/DevEditor.tsx, packages/editor/test/**, e2e/web/**, docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md, docs/lessons.md, the journal. Zero new dependencies (PRD §4).
acceptance: Unit tests per guard, named in the journal: an unchanged root yields the identical snapshot string instance and a changed root a new one; N rapid source updates inside the burst window produce one store commit and one undo entry, and an update after the window a second; a toggle and an unmount flush the pending source commit; the existing 1.6/1.7 undo and toggle suites stay green. The latency spec runs inside the ordinary `playwright test` invocation (so 1.verify.r1h runs it on all three runners) and is green; the journal records p50/p95 at 1k and 10k words for the rendered and the source view, before and after the changes, measured in this container under the spec's protocol, with the honest statement that they are one machine's numbers; `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` green; `git diff --stat` against the branch base touches only the scope files, docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md, docs/lessons.md and docs/progress/journal-main.md; no manifest or lockfile change.

description:
Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r2 H1 — Claude finding 1 blocker; H5 — Claude finding 5; H6 — Claude finding 6; the F1/G4 family in `stripUnparsableWhitespace`, packages/editor/src/schema.ts, a file of passed tasks 1.13 and 1.25, whose records are not edited): the strip's ownership rule stops at every atom and says nothing about an atom that is a block's **last** node, so a `hard_break` left at the end of a paragraph or heading reaches `format`, which writes it as a bare trailing `\` that `parse` reads back as a literal backslash — `format(parse("one\
"))` is `"one\\
"` and the `break` node is gone. Reproduction (Claude, Chromium at c9408ee): seed `hard-break.md`'s shape through the source view, `Ctrl+End`, three `Backspace` presses — the markdown pane shows `"one\
"`, `writeText` receives exactly that, the status reads "Copied Markdown", and the copied file does not round-trip (PRD §7's gate criterion). A heading whose last node is a `hard_break` is worse: `"H\

"` reparses as a paragraph, the block type lost (H5). Every one of 1.25's eleven boundary guards asserts whitespace, never an atom, and both corpus legs (packages/editor/test/typing-legs.ts) only ever `insertText`, so a tree that needs a deletion to build is outside every guard. Do four things. (1) Extend the ownership rule, stated once in the doc comment: the block's end takes the trailing whitespace of its last inline node **and drops a trailing `hard_break`**, repeatedly, until the last node is neither a whitespace-only run nor a break — a break with nothing after it is not a line break (CommonMark §6.7: a backslash at a paragraph's end is a literal backslash), dropped the way a run trimmed to nothing is dropped; a block that is only a break becomes an empty block, whatever the empty block's existing fixed point is (state it). (2) The cell clause (H6): a GFM cell cannot hold a line ending (the row would end), so inside a `table_cell` a line-ending run collapses to one space rather than to `
`; the cell's own two ends stay boundary 11. (3) Guards in packages/editor/test/editor-fixed-point.test.ts, one per position, each asserting `format(root)` bytes and `format(parse(format(root))) === format(root)`: a break as the block's last node, a block that is only a break, a break followed only by whitespace — each on `paragraph` and on `heading` (the heading's guard pins the block type separately); a line ending inside a cell serialises without `
`. (4) The class (DECISIONS #review-1-r2, Claude's lesson 2): a third `editor fixed point` corpus leg in the same file, titled for **deletion**, that for every fixture in fixtures/markdown/index.json applies deletion-shaped transactions (`tr.delete`, the call a `Backspace` makes) — delete the whole inline content after every `hard_break`, so the break becomes its block's last node; delete the last character of every block's last text run, so a run can empty and the block end can land on an atom or an inline-code run — and asserts `format(pmToMdast(doc))` is a parse∘format fixed point; the existing two legs unchanged; the journal states how many fixtures each deletion reached (from the loop, never a literal). Playwright on /dev/editor, in e2e/web/editor-soft-line-breaks.spec.ts or a new spec: the reproduction above as a case that deletes rather than types — after the three `Backspace` presses the markdown pane reads `one
` and the spy-recorded copy equals it; a heading variant; and, for H6, a multi-line plain-text paste into a table cell (the route the typing keymap does not consume) asserting the pane holds one space and no `
` — if no browser route reaches a cell's line ending, say so in the journal and keep the unit guard. Scope: packages/editor/src/schema.ts, packages/editor/test/**, e2e/web/**, docs/lessons.md, the journal. Zero new dependencies (PRD §4). A defect found outside this scope gets a docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md line with a revisit trigger and a hard stop in this task's commit, never only a lesson or a test comment (DECISIONS #review-1-r1). description: Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r2 H8 — Sol finding 2, filed against docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md:44 and reconciled as a required should-fix: the r1 deferral of the ` ` family's emphasis-edge member rested on the claim that it is unreachable while Phase 1 binds no mark-toggle command, and the claim is false). Reproduction (Sol, `/report/probe.mjs`, ordinary keyboard events): load `a *b* c`, put the rendered caret immediately after `b`, type a space → the pane reads `a *b * c`. Marks come from input rules and from every loaded file, and a caret at the end of an emphasised word sits inside the mark, so this is a one-keystroke route in the rendered view to the byte family Michael escalated at r0 (DECISIONS #review-1-r0 F1). Cause: `emphasis[text("b ")]` is a tree no Markdown file parses to — a closing `*` must be right-flanking (CommonMark §6.2: not preceded by Unicode whitespace) — and the serializer's `unsafe` table faithfully spells the difference as a character reference. Fix, in `stripUnparsableWhitespace` (packages/editor/src/schema.ts; a file of passed tasks 1.13 and 1.25, whose records are not edited) or a sibling it calls: the mark-edge clause of the ownership rule, stated once in the doc comment — ASCII whitespace at the outer edge of an `emphasis`, `strong` or `strikethrough` run belongs **outside** the mark: a marked run's leading whitespace is moved before the mark and its trailing whitespace after it, merged into the unmarked neighbour where there is one (so `text("a "), em("b "), text("c")` becomes `text("a "), em("b"), text(" c")`); a run that is whitespace-only loses those marks; nested marks give up the whitespace from every mark whose edge it touches; a link's text keeps its whitespace (`[b ](u)` is a link) and inline code stays opaque; the moved whitespace then falls under the existing line and block rules, so the clause runs first. Enumerate the edges from §6.2's flanking rules, not from the reproduction: leading edge, trailing edge, both, whitespace-only, for each of the three marks, plus a nested case (`strong` inside `emphasis`, whitespace at the shared edge) and the link absence case — one guard per case in packages/editor/test/editor-fixed-point.test.ts, first, middle and last positions in the block for the trailing-edge case, each asserting `format(root)` bytes, `not.toContain(" ")` and the parse∘format fixed point. A fourth `editor fixed point` corpus leg in the same file, titled for the mark edge: for every fixture in fixtures/markdown/index.json, insert one space at the end of every text node carrying `emphasis`, `strong` or `strikethrough` (inside the mark — `insertText` with the node's marks, the shape a caret inside the mark produces), and assert the output is a parse∘format fixed point, contains no ` `, and differs from `format(parse(x))` only by spaces; the existing legs unchanged. Playwright on /dev/editor: Sol's reproduction as a case — `a *b* c` loaded, caret after `b`, one space → the pane reads `a *b* c\n`; the absence case (a space typed after the closing delimiter, outside the mark) unchanged; and one case that types `*word*` from nothing (the input rule) followed by a space, asserting the pane reads `*word*\n` whichever tree the input rule leaves the caret in. Scope: packages/editor/src/schema.ts, packages/editor/test/**, e2e/web/**, docs/lessons.md, the journal. Zero new dependencies (PRD §4). A defect found outside this scope gets a docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md line with a revisit trigger and a hard stop in this task's commit, never only a lesson or a test comment (DECISIONS #review-1-r1). acceptance: One guard per edge-and-mark case enumerated above, each asserting `format` bytes, the absence of ` ` and the fixed point, listed in the journal; the mark-edge leg green for every fixture in the index (count from the index, never a literal), non-vacuous (the journal states how many marked runs the corpus holds, from the loop), and asserted able to fail (the clause disabled by a test-local shim goes red — recorded, not committed); the existing guards and the other three legs green and unchanged in meaning; the three Playwright cases green, with `grep -rn ' ' e2e/web packages/editor/test` naming only assertions of absence; the schema-roundtrip, roundtrip, parse-dom and clipboard suites green; `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` green; every e2e/web spec green in the container; `git diff --stat` against the branch base touches only the scope files, docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md (only if a line is added), docs/lessons.md and docs/progress/journal-main.md; no manifest or lockfile change.

description: Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r2 H2 — Sol finding 1 blocker; the seam of passed tasks 1.17 and 1.24, whose records are not edited): a flush inside a continuous source typing burst splits undo history when the continuation outlasts one coalescing window. Reproduction (Sol, `/report/probe.mjs` and `probe.log`): blank /dev/editor, toggle to source, type `a`, click Copy Markdown, return the caret to the source view, type `bcdef` at 300 ms per character, press Ctrl+Z at once → `a` remains (Ctrl+Shift+Z restores `abcdef`); the same burst without the Copy (`control.mjs`) undoes to empty. Sol's keystroke times: 242, 308, 612, 924, 1237, 1543 ms — every adjacent gap under 314 ms, the two commits' keystroke times 1,300 ms apart. Cause: `bindCodeMirror` (packages/editor/src/toggle.ts) keeps one time for the pending segment, `pendingAt`, its **latest** keystroke, and `push` (packages/core/src/undo.ts) decides continuity by one distance, `at - present.at` — the previous entry's last keystroke against the segment's last keystroke — so the adjacent keystrokes between them are invisible, and 1.24's grouping rule (the chain of keystrokes that becomes one commit is the chain that became one coalesced entry before 1.17) holds only for a segment shorter than the window; 1.24's case 3 stops its continuation at 200 ms and never reaches this. Fix: the pending segment carries both its first and its last keystroke time; continuity is decided between the segment's **first** keystroke and the previous entry's last, and the entry keeps the **last** for the next comparison. Thread it through the contract rather than around it: `PushOptions` (core) gains `from` — the earliest keystroke of the batch, defaulting to `at` — and `push` merges when `from` is within the window of the present entry's `at` (a clock that went backwards still starts a new step); the store's `commit` passes it through; the binding records the first keystroke time when a segment opens and the latest on every `change`, and its commit carries both; the rendered view and every other caller are unchanged (`from` defaults to `at`). Restate the grouping rule in the module comment (it is stated once; make it true again: continuity is a property of adjacent keystrokes, so a segment is continuous with the previous entry when its first keystroke is, however long the segment runs). Explicit closure on a toggle and on a history command (`endCoalescing`, `beforeHistory`) is preserved. Tests with the injected clock (`now` and `schedule` options), one per case, named in the journal: (a) a commit, then a continuation whose total duration exceeds the window while every adjacent gap is under it, ending by the timer — one undo entry; (b) the same continuation ending by a flush — one entry; (c) a continuation whose first keystroke lands more than a window after the previous commit — two entries, whether timed or flushed (the genuine-gap absence case); (d) the 1.24 cases unchanged and green; (e) a core test in packages/core/test for `from`: presence (merges when `from` is inside the window and `at` is outside) and absence (`from` omitted behaves as before). Playwright in e2e/web/editor-toggle.spec.ts (the 1.24 reproductions are the model): Sol's reproduction as real chords with `delay: 300` — after Ctrl+Z the pane and the surface are empty; after Ctrl+Shift+Z they read `abcdef\n`. G9's revisit trigger fires here (DECISIONS #review-1-r1 G9: the first task that changes `bindCodeMirror`'s commit path after 1.24): add the third reported line to e2e/web/latency.spec.ts's source-view measurement — `commit: p50/p95, n=<bursts>`, the deferred whole-buffer `parse` at the burst boundary — evidence only, no threshold, reported the way the existing two lines are. Scope: packages/core/src/undo.ts, packages/core/test/**, packages/editor/src/store.ts, packages/editor/src/toggle.ts, packages/editor/test/**, e2e/web/**, docs/lessons.md, the journal. Zero new dependencies (PRD §4). A defect found outside this scope gets a docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md line with a revisit trigger and a hard stop in this task's commit, never only a lesson or a test comment (DECISIONS #review-1-r1). Procedure note (DECISIONS #review-1-r2 H7): this task's generated `PROMPT.md` wrapper still lists the pre-1.verify.r2 iteration steps (implement, then one journal entry, one commit); CLAUDE.md's stub-first `## Every iteration` list is the one that stands — the wrapper's own line 1 says CLAUDE.md outranks it, the mismatch is mechanical (commit granularity), and it is not a conflict to stop on — so stub the journal, commit, implement, complete the stub.
acceptance: One unit test per case (a)–(e), green, each named in the journal against its case; the Playwright reproduction green and asserted able to fail (the `from` carried by the binding's commit replaced by its `at` in a scratch edit turns it red — recorded, reverted before the commit); the 1.6/1.7/1.17/1.24 undo, toggle and burst suites unchanged in meaning and green (a changed expectation is explained in the journal against the grouping rule); the latency spec prints the `commit` line for the source view at both sizes and the journal quotes it; `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` green; every e2e/web spec green in the container; `git diff --stat` against the branch base touches only the scope files, docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md (only if a line is added), docs/lessons.md and docs/progress/journal-main.md; no manifest or lockfile change.

description: Phase 1 review fix, tests and one comment (DECISIONS #review-1-r2 H3 — Claude finding 2; H4 — Claude finding 3, a consequence of #021's scope decision; H9 — Grok finding 1). (a) H3: the flush `toggle` performs before it reads the store (apps/desktop/src/dev/DevEditor.tsx:102, `sourceBinding.current?.flush()`) has no test that fails without it — Claude replaced the line with a comment and the full e2e/web suite stayed 68/68 — and found no behavioural difference either, which points at the line being redundant with `SourceBinding.destroy`'s own `commitPending()` on the mode-change effect cleanup (the cleanup runs before the rendered view is built), while the comment at :98-101 asserts an ordering (the pending commit before `toggleMode` closes the group) that the line may no longer be the cause of. `toggle` is the first reader named by the rule 1.verify.r2 promoted into CLAUDE.md (every reader of the store that is not an editing surface settles the pending source burst before it reads, and a new reader's test is an action inside the coalescing window) and the one of the four readers without such a case. Do this in order and record each step: add the toggle-inside-the-window case to e2e/web/editor-toggle.spec.ts — toggle to source, type inside the window, toggle back with no wait, assert the rendered document and the markdown pane hold the burst; then run the mutation against both candidate guards, separately — first `:102` removed, then `destroy`'s `commitPending()` removed — and record which cases go red under each; look for the ordering case the comment claims (a burst typed in source inside the window, a toggle at once, a keystroke in the rendered view at once, one Undo: if the group closed before the burst was committed, the burst and the keystroke could share an entry) and add it if it distinguishes the two; keep `:102` only if some case fails without it, otherwise rewrite its comment to say that `destroy`'s flush on the effect cleanup is what settles the burst and that this call is the reader's own statement of the rule — no other source change. The journal names the test that discharges the toggle clause of the promoted rule. (b) H4: `installWriteTextSpy` is the first statement of `openEditor` in e2e/web/editor-clipboard.spec.ts, the only route to `clickCopyMarkdown`, so every click of Copy Markdown in the suite goes to a stub that always resolves and nothing exercises the real clipboard write; in this container the unspied click fails with `Copy failed: the browser refused clipboard access` unless the permission is granted, so the `catch` branch is reachable in CI's environment and covered by nothing. Keep the three spy cases byte-exact as they are (#021, 1.28); add one case that grants `clipboard-read` and `clipboard-write`, opens the editor **without** the spy (a second opener or an option on `openEditor`, never a spy that is installed and then bypassed), types a word, clicks Copy Markdown, and asserts only that the status becomes "Copied Markdown" and that `navigator.clipboard.readText()` **contains** the word — platform-independent (a carriage return does not break "contains"; no normalisation, no `process.platform`, no carriage-return escape in code — 1.28's grep guards stay at their counts except that `readText` now appears in exactly this one case, named in its doc comment), still red if `writeText` rejects. Extend the describe block's doc comment: a copy test asserts the string the app wrote; one case asserts the real write resolves and the OS holds the word; a paste test of foreign content is the one that needs the real clipboard for its source. (c) H9: packages/editor/test/position-map-editor-leg.test.ts:180 asserts `names.length === Object.keys(index).length` where `names` is `Object.keys(index).sort()` — `x === x`, the class 1.21 (F9c) and 1.26 (G8) removed from the neighbouring files; drop the tautology and leave `expect(names.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` and the `blockEndChecked`/`inBlockChecked` collectors as the coverage claim. Scope: apps/desktop/src/dev/DevEditor.tsx (the one line and its comment only), e2e/web/**, packages/editor/test/position-map-editor-leg.test.ts, docs/lessons.md, the journal. description: Phase 1 verification-gate repair, test-only (repair after the 1.verify.r3h GATE-FAILED, ci.yml run 34563964087 at 32552e0: ubuntu-latest and windows-latest green on every unit test and every e2e/web spec, 79 Playwright cases each; macos-latest green on every unit test and on every e2e/web case except one — `e2e/web/editor-mark-edge.spec.ts` › `a space typed at a mark edge never reaches the Markdown as a character reference` › "H8 (Sol's reproduction): `a *b* c`, the caret after `b`, one space — the space lands inside the mark and the pane is clean" — whose first `expectClean(page, "a *b* c\n")` (the call at spec line 78) timed out receiving `a *b* c\n`, the seed's own bytes unchanged; the log is /logs/ci/1.verify.r3h/a1/workflow.log, step `test (macos-latest)` › `Playwright (e2e/web)`; DECISIONS #022). Principal reading, to be confirmed from that log and the spec before anything changes, never assumed: the case places the caret with `page.keyboard.press("ControlOrMeta+Home")` — Meta+Home on macOS — and three `ArrowRight`. On ubuntu and windows Ctrl+Home is Blink's document-start motion; on macOS a Home, End or modifier chord in a contenteditable is resolved by the OS's key-binding layer (Cocoa scrolls on Home and End, document motion is Cmd+Arrow), so the chord did not put the caret at the document start, the three `ArrowRight` had nothing to traverse from where `seedFromSource`'s click had left the caret (the paragraph's end), the space was typed after `c`, and the trailing-whitespace clause of `stripUnparsableWhitespace` removed it — exactly the received bytes. The assertion meant to catch that, `expect(page.locator(".ProseMirror em")).toHaveText("b ")`, cannot: `toHaveText` normalises whitespace, so `b` satisfies it; and the pane assertion `a *b* c` is the same bytes whether the space was typed inside the mark (moved out by the clause) or outside it after the delimiter, so on no runner did the case prove that the keystroke built Sol's tree. Two defects, both in the test; the app is not implicated (the clause of 1.30 is exercised by the unit guards and the corpus leg in packages/editor/test/editor-fixed-point.test.ts). Fix both, in e2e/web/editor-mark-edge.spec.ts only. (1) Place the caret through motions Blink alone decides, which the Linux container therefore proves for every OS: arrow keys — in a one-line block `ArrowUp` reaches the block's start and `ArrowDown` its end in Blink on every OS (Sol's route with the OS-decided key removed: /logs/reviews/1/r2/sol/probe.mjs line 6 is a bare `Home`, three `ArrowRight`, a typed space, on Linux), then the `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` counts the cases already use; if the container shows `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` not reaching the block's edges, the fallback is a click at a computed point of the ``'s bounding box (its last pixel puts the caret after `b`), stated in the doc comment. Never a `Home` or `End` key and never a `ControlOrMeta+` chord in the rendered view; state the rule once in the file's doc comment in words. The absence case's `ControlOrMeta+End` (spec line 101) is the same construct and is replaced the same way — it passed on macOS only because the seed's click had already left the caret at the end. (2) Every assertion on the ``'s text is byte-exact: `textContent()` compared with `toBe("b ")` in the H8 case (the space went inside the mark; the document keeps it there and the clause runs on the way out) and `toBe("b")` in the absence case, and, for the input-rule case that by its title accepts either tree, an explicit regex naming both (`/^word ?$/` after the space, `toBe("word")` after the `x`) — never `toHaveText`, which normalises whitespace and is the assertion that let the miss through. Do not branch on `process.platform`, do not `.skip`, do not widen any poll timeout, do not touch `stripUnparsableWhitespace` or DevEditor. Scope: e2e/web/editor-mark-edge.spec.ts plus docs/lessons.md and the journal; no source edits, no config edits, no workflow edits, zero new dependencies (PRD §4). The same construct in the rendered view of two other spec files (editor-soft-line-breaks.spec.ts lines 85 and 107, editor-trailing-break.spec.ts lines 125 and 138) is outside this task's scope and already on docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md (the #022 line); the bare `Home`/`End` in the source view (editor-cursor.spec.ts, editor-toggle.spec.ts) is CodeMirror's own keymap and not a member; leave those files untouched, and a defect found outside this scope gets a docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md line with a revisit trigger and a hard stop in this task's commit (DECISIONS #review-1-r1). The spec is a file of passed task 1.30, not its record (DECISIONS #016); the repair is authorised by this task. Each attempt appends its own `- [] ` journal line to docs/progress/journal-main.md — an earlier attempt's line stays as it is; completing an earlier attempt's stub and appending nothing is `NO-JOURNAL` even with DONE printed and the suite green (lesson [1.29]). description: Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r3 I3 — Claude finding 2, should-fix required, a regression introduced by 1.30; I4 — Claude finding 3, pre-existing since 1.13; `stripUnparsableWhitespace` and `giveUpEdges` in packages/editor/src/schema.ts, a file of passed tasks whose records are not edited): link-marked text is not opaque to the strip's trims where the link's own edge is the trim's edge. (I3) The mark-edge clause splits a **link-marked** run at a flanking mark's edge and the split-off whitespace keeps the `link` mark, so a link with edge whitespace inside emphasis/strong/strikethrough — a tree `parse` produces from valid Markdown — comes back trimmed with a second, whitespace-only link invented: reproduced by the reconciliation with no transaction at all (`mdastToPM` → `pmToMdast` → `format`): `*a [b ](u)* c` → `*a [b](u)*[ ](u) c`; `**a [b ](u)** c` → `**a [b](u)**[ ](u) c`; `x *[ b](u)*` → `x [ *b*](u)`; in a cell `| *[b ](u)* |` → `| [*b*](u) |`; byte-identical at c9408ee (before 1.30). Cause: CommonMark's flanking rule reads the delimiter's actual neighbour, which is `)` or `[` when the link's edge coincides with the run's edge — the whitespace inside the link text is not at a flanking edge — but ProseMirror's flat mark set (`[link, emphasis]` on one node) cannot say which mark is outermost, and the clause assumed the flanking mark. (I4) The end-of-block loop and the line-start trim drop a link's edge whitespace at a **block** boundary: `see [the essay ](u)` → `see [the essay](u)`; `[ b](u)` → `[b](u)`; `# [b ](u)` → `# [b](u)` (reproduced the same way; micromark keeps `[b ](u)`, so these are silent rewrites of the user's link text, fixed points but not identity). Do three things. (1) The link predicate, stated once in the doc comment beside the ownership rule: in `giveUpEdges`, when the edge node carries `link` and the node beyond the run on that side does not carry the same link (the link's edge coincides with the run's edge), the scan stops there — the delimiter's neighbour is the bracket, nothing has to move; when the link continues past the run (`[*b* c](u)`, the existing guard) the space still moves within the link, as now. In the end-of-block loop and the line-start trim, a text node carrying `link` stops the trim (the block's end is then the link's `)`); inline code stays opaque as before. (2) Guards in packages/editor/test/editor-fixed-point.test.ts, each asserting `format(root)` equals the input's canonical bytes and that `parse(format(root))` holds exactly one `link`: `*[b ](u)*`, `*[ b](u)*`, `*a [b ](u)* c` at the first, middle and last positions of the block, the strong and strikethrough twins, the cell; `[b ](u)` last and `[ b](u)` first in a paragraph, a heading and a cell; the `[*b* c](u)` guard unchanged. (3) The class: a fifth corpus leg in typing-legs.ts, titled for the **link edge**, that types a space at the end of every **link-marked** text node over every fixture (the `link` mark is not inclusive, so the leg passes the node's marks to `insertText` explicitly, as the mark-edge leg does) and asserts the fixed point, the link count and no numeric character reference; a fixture fixtures/markdown/link-in-emphasis.md (agent-written: a link with edge whitespace inside emphasis, a bare link with edge whitespace at a block end, with its canonical sibling and index entry) so the legs reach the trees. Playwright on /dev/editor: Claude's reproduction (load `*a [b ](u)* c`, type one letter, the pane and the spy's copy hold exactly one link and the canonical bytes) with the caret placed only through motions Blink decides (DECISIONS #022). |` in any literal or a `break` — whatever the item's flag says, exactly as for two paragraphs, so a tight item `[paragraph("a"), heading(depth 1, "h
x"), list]` serialises as `- a

  h
  x
  =
  - i
` while `parse` reads the item as spread and writes `…=

  - i
` — reproduced by the reconciliation headlessly (`fixed: false`); I2's class, one pair short. packages/editor/test/list-spread.test.ts's `KINDS.heading` is ATX depth 2 with `text("h")` and no break, so its 225 pairs cannot see it. Route: the heading input rule typed at the start of a hard-wrapped second paragraph of a list item that has a nested list after it — reachable, not ordinary. Do two things. (1) In `needsBlankLine`'s paragraph clause, `right.type === "heading"` and the same predicate `formatHeadingAsSetext` uses (depth ≤ 2, non-empty text, a line ending in any literal descendant or a `break`), stated in the doc comment's pair list as item 1's fourth member; the rule stays confirmed against `parse(format(·))` by the enumeration, never assumed. (2) The two setext variants added to `KINDS` (a depth-1 heading with `
` in its text; a depth-2 heading with a `break`), so the pair test asserts them by construction; one guard with the nested list present and one absent, each asserting `format(root)`'s bytes and the fixed point; the existing 225 pairs and every identity leg green with every fixture byte-identical. Scope: packages/editor/src/schema.ts (`needsBlankLine` and its doc comment only), packages/editor/test/list-spread.test.ts, docs/lessons.md, the journal. No other source change, no fixture change, no config or workflow edits, zero new dependencies (PRD §4). A defect found outside this scope gets a docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md line with a revisit trigger and a hard stop in this task's commit, never only a lesson or a test comment (DECISIONS #review-1-r1). Each attempt appends its own `- [<id>] ` journal line to docs/progress/journal-main.md, stubbed first by one command that prints the timestamp — an earlier attempt's line stays as it is; completing an earlier attempt's stub and appending nothing is `NO-JOURNAL` even with DONE printed and the suite green (lesson [1.29]). Procedure note (DECISIONS #review-1-r2 H7): this task's generated `PROMPT.md` wrapper still lists the pre-1.verify.r2 iteration steps (implement, then one journal entry, one commit); CLAUDE.md's stub-first `## Every iteration` list is the one that stands — the wrapper's own line 1 says CLAUDE.md outranks it, the mismatch is mechanical (commit granularity), and it is not a conflict to stop on — so stub the journal, commit, implement, complete the stub.
acceptance: The two `KINDS` entries present and the pair enumeration green over them (its pair count grows from the loop, never a literal); the two guards green and listed in the journal; the clause's able-to-fail recorded (the clause disabled by a test-local shim goes red on the setext pair — recorded, not committed); every identity leg green with every fixture byte-identical; the list-split and paste legs green unchanged; `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` green; every e2e/web spec green in the container; no manifest or lockfile change; zero new dependencies (PRD §4). `git diff --stat` against the branch base touches only the scope files, docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md (only if a line is added), docs/lessons.md and docs/progress/journal-main.md.

description:

Reproduced by the reconciliation headlessly: `abc\` newline `def`, `def` deleted → the editor's paragraph is `abc` + `hard_break`, the mdast paragraph `abc`, and `toSource` of the position after the break is `{ line: 1, ch: 0 }`; Sol's browser probe: load `abc\` newline `def`, click the end (asserted `def`, offset 3), Backspace ×3, toggle to source, type `X` → the pane is `Xabc
`, not `abcX
`. Task 1.37 pinned both shapes as `it.fails` ("known defect") and deferred the fix on its test-only scope; the reconciliation takes it now. Do three things. (1) In `toSource`, the no-spelling branch for a block correspondence answers `afterLastNode(entries, map, pos)` — the last inline node ending at or before `pos` — instead of the block's start: `3:2`-shaped answers for shape (a), the end of the paragraph before the placeholder for shape (b); the existing atom behaviour (`delimiterPosition`, a position on a mark's delimiters, a node answered with its own start when it is the innermost *inline* node) unchanged, stated in the doc comment as the third clause of the mapping. (2) In position-map-editor-leg.test.ts: the width branch and the split collector the `[1.37]` backlog line names deleted, both shapes folded into clause 3 of the deletion leg as ordinary passing assertions (the cursor placed after a dropped break and inside a split item's empty paragraph maps to the byte end of what precedes it), the `it.fails` case removed — the suite then reports no expected failure — and the reach assertions kept (`blocksEndingPastCorrespondence > 0`, `splitParagraphsPastCorrespondence > 0`, now as ordinary counts of shapes the clause covered). Asserted able to fail, recorded in the journal and not committed: `:351`'s old answer restored under a test-local shim goes red on shape (a) and on shape (b). (3) Sol's reproduction as a Playwright case in e2e/web/editor-toggle.spec.ts (or a new spec if the file's fixture helpers do not fit): load `abc\` newline `def
`, click the paragraph's end and assert `{ text: "def", offset: 3 }`, Backspace ×3, `ControlOrMeta+/` to source (the toggle chord, not a caret motion — the guard allows it), type `X`, Copy Markdown → the pane and the spy `abcX
`; the split-item sibling asserted headless in (2) only. description:
Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r5 K1 — Claude finding 1 blocker, Sol finding 1 blocker; packages/core/src/format.ts, a file of passed Phase 0 tasks and of task 1.40, whose records are not edited — a new task per DECISIONS #016): the astral (non-BMP) neighbour of a flanking mark is written as a lone-surrogate character reference. `mdast-util-to-markdown/lib/util/container-phrasing.js` (2.1.2; read it in node_modules first, with lib/handle/emphasis.js, lib/handle/root.js, lib/util/encode-info.js and micromark-util-classify-character/index.js) rewrites a child's output after its handler returned at exactly two places: the first UTF-16 unit of the child after an attention run (`if (encodeAfter && encodeAfter === value.slice(0, 1)) value = encodeCharacterReference(encodeAfter.charCodeAt(0)) + value.slice(1)`) and the last unit of the child before it (`results[results.length - 1].slice(0, -1) + encodeCharacterReference(before.charCodeAt(0))`), where `after` is the first unit of the next child's output (a speculative `handle`/`peek` call, `.charAt(0)`) and `before` the last unit of the previous one. A character outside the BMP directly outside `*`, `**` or `~~` whose inner edge is punctuation or whitespace is therefore encoded one unit wide: `x ~~a.~~😀` → `x ~~a.~~��
`, `😀~~(a)~~ x` → `��~~(a)~~ x
`, `x ~~a ~~😀` → `x ~~a ~~��
