description:
Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r6 L1 — Sol finding 1 blocker, Grok finding 1 blocker; packages/core/src/format.ts, a file of passed tasks 1.40 and 1.45, whose records are not edited — a new task per DECISIONS #016): an astral (non-BMP) character that is the closing neighbour of one flanking run and the opening neighbour of the next is written as two lone-surrogate references. `mdast-util-to-markdown/lib/util/container-phrasing.js` (2.1.2) makes its two post-handler rewrites on the *same* text child when that child sits between two runs whose inner edges are punctuation: `encodeAfter` encodes the child's first UTF-16 unit after the left run and `encodingInfo.before` encodes its last unit before the right run, so a one-character astral child comes out as `��` — a form task 1.45's `SPLIT_PAIR` does not match, because it accepts only a reference beside a *raw* mate. Reproduced by the reconciliation headlessly at c2f6526 in a detached scratch worktree: `format(parse("*a.*😀*(b)*
"))` is `*a.*��*(b)*
`, whose parse holds `a.` U+FFFD U+FFFD `(b)`, for every mark pair of `*`, `**`, `~~` (nine pairs, mixed pairs included) × 😀 (U+1F600), 𐐀 (U+10400), 𝕒 (U+1D552), in a paragraph, a heading, a table cell, a link's text, a blockquote and a list item — 27 + 5 trees, none a fixed point, every one leaving the neighbour `unresolved` in `formatWithMap` (path `0.1` in a paragraph) because the map's retry (task 1.46) names the code-point reference `😀` and not the two-unit form; the BMP twin `*a.*b*(b)*` and the whitespace-inner twin `x *a *😀* b* y` are fixed points (the second keeps the raw emoji: no encoding is decided for it). Sol's browser route (`/logs/reviews/1/r6/sol/between-browser.mjs`, its log beside it): load `*a.* 😀 *(b)*`, delete the two spaces around the emoji with ordinary caret motion, Copy Markdown — the rendered text still shows the emoji, the status reports success, the clipboard holds the corrupt form. The 1.45 "both sides" guard (`strikethrough-flanking.test.ts:394–401`, `😀~~(a.)~~😀`) is two different emoji, each split once, which `SPLIT_PAIR` handles; no guard puts one scalar between two runs. Prototyped by the reconciliation and taken (the suite 3,298 green with it): add a third alternative to `SPLIT_PAIR` — a high-surrogate reference (`&#xD[89AB]..;`) directly followed by a low-surrogate reference (`&#xD[C-F]..;`) — and widen it with the same code-point arithmetic `widenSplitSurrogateReferences` already uses; nothing else changes: `classifyCharacter`, `encodeInfo`, `handleDelete`, the root handler and the wrapper's installation stay as 1.45 left them, and the doc comments of `SPLIT_PAIR` and `widenSplitSurrogateReferences` are rewritten to name three forms, derived from the two rewrites of container-phrasing.js and their join on one two-unit child (DECISIONS #review-1-r4 J2: from the branches, read in node_modules). With the bytes whole, `placeChildren`'s existing one-code-point candidate (positions.ts, task 1.46) finds the neighbour — assert it, change no code in positions.ts. Do three things. (1) The regex and its callback in format.ts as above. (2) Guards in packages/core/test/strikethrough-flanking.test.ts, a new describe "one astral character between two flanking runs": every ordered pair of `emphasis`, `strong`, `delete` (nine) × the three astral characters above, each tree `paragraph(mark1(text("a.")), text(c), mark2(text("(b)")))`, asserting `format(root)`'s bytes with `toBe` (the code-point reference between the two runs), that the bytes parse to exactly two marks of the named types, that the parsed tree's text values joined equal the built tree's (the instrument that sees U+FFFD), the parse∘format fixed point, and `formatWithMap(root).map.unresolved` empty; the same tree once in each of a heading, a table cell, a link's text, a blockquote and a list item (one pair, one character each — the wrapper is on `state.containerPhrasing` and the cell's assembler calls it, `mdast-util-gfm-table/lib/index.js`); the absence cases: the BMP twin (`b`, one reference, unchanged) and the whitespace-inner twin (the raw emoji kept); the 1.45 both-sides guard unchanged; the five new sources `*a.*😀*(b)*`, `**a.**𐐀**(b)**`, `~~a.~~𝕒~~(b)~~`, `**a.**😀~~(b)~~`, `# *a.*😀*(b)*` added to the invariant-A list (each formatting to itself). Asserted able to fail, recorded in the journal and not committed: the third alternative removed goes red on the pair guards with the two-reference bytes it produces (record them). (3) A fixture fixtures/markdown/astral-between-runs.md of exactly three blocks — the paragraph `*a.*😀*(b)*`, the paragraph `**a.**𐐀~~(b)~~`, the heading `# ~~a.~~𝕒~~(b)~~` — with its canonical sibling (`format(parse(·))`, byte-identical to the source) and its index.json entry, so the identity corpus, every corpus leg and the position-map family ("maps every node of the tree, and nothing is unresolved", the rule promoted at 1.verify.r6) cover the shape; count from the index, never a literal. (4) One Playwright case in a new e2e/web/editor-astral-between-runs.spec.ts on `/dev/editor` with the `writeText` spy of 1.28 (helpers copied from editor-astral-neighbour.spec.ts and editor-toggle-encoded-neighbour.spec.ts; a spec file is self-contained): Sol's route — load `*a.* 😀 *(b)*
` through the fixture-file input, click the paragraph, `ArrowUp` (a one-line block's start), counted `ArrowRight` to the anchor asserted as `{ text: " 😀 ", offset: 1 }` (assert whatever the DOM reports and record it in the journal), `Backspace`, then the anchor asserted again, `ArrowRight` past the emoji (two UTF-16 units are one caret step in Blink — assert the offset, do not assume it), `Delete`, Copy Markdown → the pane and the spy receive `*a.*😀*(b)*
` (`toBe`), that string a fixed point of `format(parse(·))` computed in the page, its parse's text values joined equal to the paragraph's `textContent` (`a.😀(b)`), two `<em>` elements, and `&#xD` absent from the pane. Caret placement only by the click, `ArrowUp` and counted horizontal arrows with the anchor asserted before every count (DECISIONS #022, #024); no Home/End key, no chord (`tests/no-caret-chords-in-e2e.test.ts` guards the file). Scope: packages/core/src/format.ts, packages/core/test/**, fixtures/markdown/astral-between-runs.md, fixtures/markdown/astral-between-runs.canonical.md, fixtures/markdown/index.json, e2e/web/editor-astral-between-runs.spec.ts, docs/lessons.md, the journal. No positions.ts change, no editor change, no other fixture change, no config or workflow edits, zero new dependencies (PRD §4). Each attempt appends a NEW `- [<id>] ` journal line to docs/progress/journal-main.md, stubbed first by one `printf` that prints the timestamp (`printf -- '- [%s] %s Task: …' <id> "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"`) and completed in place before the commit that prints DONE — an earlier attempt's line is never edited; completing an earlier attempt's stub and appending nothing is `NO-JOURNAL` even with DONE printed and the suite green (lessons [1.29], [1.41]). Run the suite once: after the implementation is complete, `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` and the e2e/web suite each one time, then complete the stub, commit and print DONE — the runner re-runs the whole suite on the squashed candidate (RUNNER-SPEC §4), and a second verification pass in the same attempt is what the r5 and r6 chains' turn caps were spent on (lessons [1.41], [1.42], [1.47]). A defect found outside this scope gets a docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md line with a revisit trigger and a hard stop in this task's commit, never only a lesson or a test comment (DECISIONS #review-1-r1). Procedure note (DECISIONS #review-1-r2 H7): this task's generated `PROMPT.md` wrapper still lists the pre-1.verify.r2 iteration steps (implement, then one journal entry, one commit); CLAUDE.md's stub-first `## Every iteration` list is the one that stands — the wrapper's own line 1 says CLAUDE.md outranks it, the mismatch is mechanical (commit granularity), and it is not a conflict to stop on — so stub the journal, commit, implement, complete the stub.
acceptance: The pair guards green for every ordered pair of the three marks × the three astral characters and listed in the journal against their (mark1, mark2, character) tuple, each asserting bytes, two marks, the parsed text values equal to the tree's, the fixed point and `unresolved` empty; the five position-class guards green; both absence cases and the 1.45 both-sides guard green; the five new invariant-A sources format to themselves; the able-to-fail mutation recorded with the two-reference bytes it produced; `grep -c 'D\[C-F\]' packages/core/src/format.ts` is at least 2 (the third alternative present); `classifyCharacter`, `encodeInfo`, `handleDelete`, `handleRoot` and `installSurrogateWidening` unchanged (`git diff` shows no change inside those five functions) and `git diff --stat` shows no change to packages/core/src/positions.ts; the fixture present with its canonical sibling and index entry, byte-identical through every identity leg and every corpus leg and resolved by the ordinary "maps every node of the tree, and nothing is unresolved" case (count from the index; `grep -lE '&#xD[89AB]' fixtures/markdown/*.canonical.md` prints nothing); the Playwright case green in the container with the anchor asserted before each count, the copied bytes asserted by `toBe`, the fixed point, the text equality and the `<em>` count (`grep -cE 'ControlOrMeta\+(Home|End)|"(Home|End)"|ArrowDown' e2e/web/editor-astral-between-runs.spec.ts` is 0); the schema-roundtrip, roundtrip, fixtures-corpus, editor-fixed-point and positions suites green with their meaning unchanged and every other fixture byte-identical; `pnpm test`'s summary shows no expected fail; `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` green; every e2e/web spec green in the container; no manifest or lockfile change; zero new dependencies (PRD §4). `git diff --stat` against the branch base touches only the scope files, docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md (only if a line is added), docs/lessons.md and docs/progress/journal-main.md.

description:
Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r6 L2 — Claude finding 1 blocker; packages/core/src/format.ts, a file of passed tasks 1.40, 1.45 and 1.49, whose records are not edited — a new task per DECISIONS #016): an autolink literal whose URL holds a backslash is written in the `<…>` autolink form with the backslash doubled, and every `parse ∘ format` doubles it again — invariant A fails on the parser's own tree. Read first, in node_modules: `mdast-util-to-markdown/lib/handle/link.js` (the autolink branch hides the construct stack — `state.stack = []` — and writes `state.containerPhrasing(node)` between `<` and `>`), `lib/util/format-link-as-autolink.js` (the decision: `!state.options.resourceLink`, a url, no title, one text child equal to the url, a protocol, no control character, space or angle bracket), `lib/util/safe.js` and `lib/unsafe.js` (the text child still goes through `safe()`, which doubles a backslash before ASCII punctuation — "typical escapes are handled in `safe`" — and applies every `unsafe` entry without an `inConstruct`, although inside an autolink no escape works: CommonMark §6.4 reads the bytes literally). Reproduced by the reconciliation headlessly at c2f6526: `parse("see https://x.y\ end
")` holds `link{url: "https://x.y\"}` and `format` writes `see <https://x.y\\> end
`, whose parse holds `url: "https://x.y\\"`, then eight backslashes, then sixteen; the same for `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo\_bar` (the hand-escaped underscore many writers put in URLs); `www.x.y\` is a fixed point because the built-in falls back to the resource form `[www.x.y\\](http://www.x.y\\)` (the text and the url differ), and the plain `https://example.com/a_b` autolink is a fixed point. In the browser (Claude's route): load `see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo\_bar end`, the rendered link's `href` is `…/Foo\_bar`, the pane and Copy Markdown hand over `<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo\\_bar>` with status "Copied Markdown" — the user's URL changed silently. The corpus's one autolink (`autolink-literal.md`) has no such character. Prototyped by the reconciliation and taken (the suite green with it): an app-owned fallback that keeps the autolink form exactly when it can carry the url and takes the resource form otherwise, per node — `[https://x.y\\](https://x.y\\)` is a fixed point whose parse holds the original url (backslash escapes work in a link destination and in a label), as the `www.` case already shows; `resourceLink: true` globally is NOT taken (it would rewrite the autolink of `autolink-literal.md` and every canonical sibling holding one; docs/MARKDOWN-STYLE.md rule 8 keeps the autolink "when the text is the destination", which this fallback preserves whenever the form can spell the destination). Do three things. (1) In format.ts, wrap the configured `link` handler once per serialization in the shape `installSurrogateWidening` uses (installed from the app `root` handler on the `State` it receives, a marker on the state, the original called bound to `state`; `mdast-util-to-markdown` is not a direct dependency of packages/core, so the built-in is reached through `state.handlers.link` and never imported): the wrapper calls the original; when the result is the autolink form (it starts with `<`) and the bytes between `<` and `>` are not byte-identical to `node.url`, it calls the original again with `state.options.resourceLink` set to `true` for that call only and restored in a `finally`, so the resource form is written for that node — the one option `formatLinkAsAutolink` reads; the wrapper's `peek` answers `[` when the fallback will be taken and the original's `peek` otherwise (the previous sibling's `after` classification reads it; both `<` and `[` are punctuation, state that in the doc comment). State the criterion once in the doc comment: the autolink form is kept exactly when it round-trips the url byte for byte, because nothing inside `<…>` can be escaped. `formatWithMap` inherits the wrapper through the app `root` handler as it inherits the widening (`configuredHandlers` captures the built-in link before the root runs and the root wraps the instrumented handler at serialization time) — confirm with one test that `formatWithMap(parse("see https://x.y\ end
"))` is a fixed point with `unresolved` empty and that the link's text child has a spelling table in which the backslash's spelling is the two-character escape. description: Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r7 M1 — Claude finding 1 blocker; packages/core/src/format.ts, a file of passed tasks 1.40, 1.45, 1.49 and 1.50, whose records are not edited — a new task per DECISIONS #016): the app's surrogate widening runs over the *joined* output of every phrasing parent, so bytes that are not a text child's are rewritten. `installSurrogateWidening` (format.ts:283–291) applies `SPLIT_PAIR`'s three forms to the whole string `containerPhrasing` returns, and the third form (task 1.49, two adjacent lone-surrogate references) is pure ASCII, so the literal bytes `��` inside a verbatim leaf are rewritten to `😀`. Reproduced by the reconciliation headlessly at 5618078 in a detached scratch worktree: ``format(parse("`��` "))`` is `` `😀` `` (the code's value changes — invariant B fails; A holds from the second pass), the same for ``see `��` here``, for inline html `a b c` (an `html` node, opaque by PRD §6.1), for a table cell holding the span, for the span inside an emphasis (`*ab `+"`��`"+` cd*`) and inside a link's text; in the browser (Claude's R1) the rendered `` shows the user's bytes while the pane, the clipboard and "Copied Markdown" carry the rewritten ones. NOT a member: a link's destination or title holding those bytes — the parser decodes a lone-surrogate reference there to U+FFFD before the serializer runs, so the tree never holds them (do not write guards for them). NOT a member either: a text child — `��` is written `\�\�`, each `&` escaped by `safe()`, which no form matches — the absence guard. Read first, in node_modules: `mdast-util-to-markdown/lib/util/container-phrasing.js` (2.1.2) whole — the look-ahead through `state.handle.handlers[type]` (lines 43–55), the eol-before-html replacement of the previous result (60–80), `encodeAfter` on the current value's first unit (88–94) and `encodingInfo.before` on the previous result's last unit (100–115), the two encodings that fire on text children only because every other handler's output begins and ends with punctuation, which `encode-info.js` never encodes; `lib/handle/emphasis.js` and `strong.js` for the inner-edge encodings a mark handler makes on its own `between` after its `containerPhrasing` returned (the app's `handleDelete` mirrors them); and `rewrittenEmissions` in packages/core/src/positions.ts, the enumeration of the same rewrites the map already holds. The fix, prototyped by the reconciliation with `pnpm lint` green and the whole unit suite green with the fixture below in the index: the wrapper widens per child, positionally, never over the join. (1) During the original `containerPhrasing` call, record each direct child's handler output by wrapping `state.handle` for that call: the wrapper calls the original and pushes `{ node, value }` when the `parent` argument is this parent (a nested call's children are its own), the zwitch function's own properties (`handlers`, `invalid`, `unknown`) copied onto the wrapper with `Object.assign` so the assembler's look-ahead still resolves, the original restored in a `finally`. (2) Walk the join with a cursor: for each recorded child, find at the cursor which form the assembler can have rewritten its output into (`startsWith`, the plain output first): for a `text` child the plain value, the first UTF-16 unit as its `&#x…;` reference, the last unit, both, and each of those with a trailing line ending replaced by one space when the next child is `html`; for every other child the plain output, plus the eol-as-space form for a `break` before `html` (task 1.58 decides that pair's bytes; this task leaves them as the parent wrote them). The guard at packages/editor/test/toggle.test.ts:1542–1548 pins the column only ("keeps task 1.52's answer") with no two-view instrument, and the 1.52 (b) Playwright route (editor-toggle-cell-end.spec.ts:179) agrees only because the input rule's `removeStoredMark` (packages/editor/src/input.ts:85) cleared the stored mark one keystroke earlier — the editor types by `storedMarks ?? $pos.marks()` (`Transaction.insertText`, read in node_modules/prosemirror-state's dist) and the map reads the doc alone. Read first: `ResolvedPos.marks()` and `Transaction.insertText` in node_modules, and `innermostAt`'s doc comment (1.53's rule). The fix, prototyped by the reconciliation with `pnpm lint` green and the whole unit suite green save the two pins named below: (1) `toSource(pos, storedMarks = null)` — a second, optional argument on `CursorMap.toSource`: the marks a character typed at `pos` receives are `storedMarks ?? $pos.marks()` (a `typedMarks` helper, `null` outside a textblock); `inlineBoundary` takes those marks instead of reading `$pos.marks()` itself, so 1.53's boundary rule is unchanged when no stored marks are given. (2) `isLeafEnd`'s block-end branch applies to a leaf without a table (an atom) and to an `inlineCode` whose typed marks do not include `schema.marks.inline_code`; an `inlineCode` at a block end whose typed marks include it is answered by its spelling table — the last offset, before the closing fence — exactly as mid-block. State the rule in `isLeafEnd`'s and `cursorMap`'s clause-3 doc comments, replacing "a space typed there is plain text, as it is in the editor", which is false for an inclusive mark. (3) The dev route's toggle (DevEditor.tsx, the `cursorMap(root, pm.state.doc).toSource(pm.state.selection.head)` call) passes `pm.state.storedMarks` as the second argument, so the caret right after the input rule closed a span still lands after the fence — the 1.52 (b) route unchanged and green. Two pins of the old answer yield, named here so they are not conflicts: packages/editor/test/toggle.test.ts:1546 ("an `inline_code` run at its block's end keeps task 1.52's answer, after the closing fence") becomes a two-view guard — with no stored marks, the column before the fence and the two views' bytes equal (``see `fooX` ``: `X` inserted in ProseMirror with `$pos.marks()` through `pmToMdast` and `format`, against `X` inserted in the source at the mapped column and reparsed); with stored marks `[]` the column after the fence and both views ``see `foo`X`` (ProseMirror inserting with the stored marks); and packages/editor/test/position-map-editor-leg.test.ts:741 (the hand-seeded `a `+"`cd`"+`` guard, "answered with that leaf's end in the bytes") with its `byteEndOf` oracle's inline-code branch: a block whose reparsed last leaf is an `inlineCode` is answered before the closing fence (the position of the value's end, `position.end.column` minus the closing fence's width — derive it from the reparsed node's bytes, never a literal), the atom branch unchanged — the deletion leg's byte clause (the character before the cursor is the block's last character) then holds for a block ending in a code span, which it did not before (probed by the reconciliation: latent because no fixture ends a block in a code span; 1.59's fixture was shaped not to). Guards in toggle.test.ts, a describe "a block-final inline code span follows the marks a typed character takes": for a paragraph, a heading, a list item, a blockquote and a table cell ending in a code span, both routes — no stored marks (the click route) and stored marks `[]` (the input-rule route) — each asserting `toSource`'s column and the two-view byte agreement (the instrument of 1.53's matrix), and the inverse `toRendered(toSource(p)) === p` over every text position of each document; 1.52's corpus inverse leg and its destructive leg green unchanged. Asserted able to fail, recorded in the journal and not committed: the block-end branch reverted to "every leaf" goes red on the no-stored-marks cases with the ``see `foo`X`` bytes it produces; the stored-marks argument ignored goes red on the stored-marks cases. One Playwright case in a new e2e/web/editor-toggle-code-span-end.spec.ts on `/dev/editor` (helpers copied from editor-toggle-cell-end.spec.ts, the `writeText` spy of 1.28 and the 200 ms tick before the chord; the click-at-a-measured-point helper copied from editor-soft-line-breaks.spec.ts, task 1.56): load ``see `foo`\n``, click at the point measured from the end of the `foo` text node's own Range rect, anchor asserted `{ text: "foo", offset: 3 }` (assert whatever the DOM reports and record it), `ControlOrMeta+/`, type `X`, toggle back, Copy Markdown → the spy's bytes ``see `fooX`\n`` with `toBe`, a fixed point, the rendered `<code>`'s `textContent` `fooX`; the existing 1.52 (b) case in editor-toggle-cell-end.spec.ts stays as it is and green (the stored-marks route). Caret placement only by a click at a computed point, `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` and counted horizontal arrows with the anchor asserted first (DECISIONS #022, #024). Scope: packages/editor/src/toggle.ts, packages/editor/test/toggle.test.ts, packages/editor/test/position-map-editor-leg.test.ts (the named guard and `byteEndOf` only), apps/desktop/src/dev/DevEditor.tsx (the one argument), e2e/web/editor-toggle-code-span-end.spec.ts, docs/lessons.md, the journal. No change to positions.ts, format.ts, schema.ts, input.ts, typing-legs.ts or any fixture, no config or workflow edits, zero new dependencies (PRD §4). Each attempt appends a NEW `- [<id>] ` journal line to docs/progress/journal-main.md, stubbed first by one `printf` that prints the timestamp (`printf -- '- [%s] %s Task: …' <id> "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"`) and completed in place before the commit that prints DONE — an earlier attempt's line is never edited; completing an earlier attempt's stub and appending nothing is `NO-JOURNAL` even with DONE printed and the suite green (lessons [1.29], [1.41]). description:
Phase 1 verification-gate repair (repair after the 1.verify.r8h GATE-FAILED, ci.yml run 35755695990 at b7f45a5: ubuntu-latest 97 passed / 1 failed and windows-latest 96 passed / 2 failed on e2e/web, macos-latest 98/98, every unit, lint and cargo step green on all three; DECISIONS #037): two of the r8 chain's new specs fail at the click that seeds the caret, before the toggle chord ever runs — `e2e/web/editor-toggle-code-span-end.spec.ts` line 127 (task 1.60; ubuntu-latest and windows-latest: expected `{ text: "foo", offset: 3 }`, received `{ text: null, offset: 4 }`) and `e2e/web/editor-toggle-cell-code-pipe.spec.ts` line 167 in `seedWithCaretAfterA` (task 1.59; windows-latest only: expected `{ text: "a|b", offset: 0 }`, received `{ text: null, offset: 0 }`). Cause, read in the installed prosemirror-view 1.42.3 (`node_modules/.pnpm/prosemirror-view@1.42.3/node_modules/prosemirror-view/dist/index.js`): a caret at either edge of a code span sits at a reveal-widget boundary — task 1.4's `.essaydown-delimiter` backticks (`packages/editor/src/reveal.ts`: the opening widget has a positive `side`, the closing one a negative `side`, and prosemirror-view gives every widget `contentEditable = "false"`) — and that one document position has two DOM spellings. Blink's hit test anchors the selection in the `` text node (`foo`/3, `a|b`/0); ProseMirror's own `NodeViewDesc.domFromPos` (line 922) spells the same position on the parent element after the closing widget (`

`/4, the value both runners received) or before the opening widget (``/0, the windows value — and the spelling the pipe spec's second case already asserts after the toggle back, where ProseMirror wrote the DOM). The two are not equivalent to ProseMirror (`scanFor` returns false at a `contentEditable == "false"` child), so which one the poll reads depends on whether the view re-synced the DOM selection after the click (`handlers.focus` schedules `selectionToDOM` 20 ms after focus when the observer's `currentSelection` differs from the DOM's, line 3904; `setSelection` at line 1025 re-spells whenever the DOM is not equivalent) — a race the 5 s poll cannot settle, because both spellings are stable and both resolve to the same document position. The precondition asserted a DOM spelling that belongs to whichever of Blink and ProseMirror wrote the DOM last; what the toggle reads is the editor's selection (`toggle` in `apps/desktop/src/dev/DevEditor.tsx` hands `pm.state.selection.head` and `pm.state.storedMarks` to `toSource`). Do exactly this. (1) Reproduce first: in the container run `e2e/web/node_modules/.bin/playwright test editor-toggle-code-span-end editor-toggle-cell-code-pipe` once before any change and record each case's outcome and received value in the journal (both were green in the container at tasks 1.59 and 1.60 and red on the gate's ubuntu-latest; record what the container shows, do not decide from it). (2) A selection readout on the dev bar, `apps/desktop/src/dev/DevEditor.tsx`: a `` beside `mode` and `status`, with no React state behind it (a state update per transaction would sit on the 1.17 latency path; the readout is written imperatively into the span through the ref), written by a small ProseMirror plugin defined in that file and added to the rendered view's `plugins` list — `new Plugin({ view: () => ({ update: (view) => write(view.state), destroy: () => clear() }) })` with `write` also called once from the plugin's `view` constructor — so that every `updateState` counts, including the store pulls `bindProseMirror` makes with `updateState` directly (a fixture load moves the selection without a dispatch). The span's text is `JSON.stringify` of `{ before, empty, marks, stored }`: `before` is `$head.parent.textBetween(0, $head.parentOffset)` (the text of the caret's own textblock before the caret, `null` when `$head.parent.isTextblock` is false), `empty` is `state.selection.empty`, `marks` is `$head.marks().map((mark) => mark.type.name)`, `stored` is `state.storedMarks === null ? null : state.storedMarks.map((mark) => mark.type.name)` — the values `toSource` and the two-view guard of DECISIONS #review-1-r7 M5 depend on. The source view leaves it empty. The plugin's doc comment names this task and the reason in two sentences. `Plugin` is imported from `prosemirror-state`, already a dependency of the app. (3) `e2e/web/editor-toggle-code-span-end.spec.ts`: keep `clickAfter` and its point unchanged; replace the `caret` poll at line 127 with a poll on the readout equal to `{ before: "see foo", empty: true, marks: ["inline_code"], stored: null }` (`before` proves the end of the span byte for byte, `marks` proves the click route's `$pos.marks()`, `stored: null` proves no stored marks — M5's click route); delete the now-unused `caret` helper; keep the 200 ms tick and its comment. Members, every one reproduced headlessly by the reconciliation at 970bb5c: `see *foo*` typed in the rendered view — the input rule's `removeStoredMark` leaves stored marks `[]` (input.ts:77–86) — then the toggle and `X`: rendered `see *foo*X`, source `see *fooX*`; strong `see **foo**X` vs `see **fooX**`; delete `see ~~foo~~X` vs `see ~~fooX~~`; the same in a heading, a list item and a table cell, and with an astral content `see *f😀*`; the click route (marks inherited, `[emphasis]`) agrees in every case and 1.60's inline-code member agrees on both routes — the controls; over the corpus, 256 block ends × 2 routes, eight block-final marked runs in six fixtures disagree on the `[]` route (astral-between-runs.md ×3, astral-neighbour.md, hard-break-in-emphasis.md, spanning-mark-last-boundary.md, spanning-mark-strikethrough.md, strikethrough-punctuation.md) and none on the click route. The other edge and the other mark, found by the reconciliation's sweep: `link` is `inclusive: false` (schema.ts:447), so at a block that starts or ends in a link the typed marks are `[]` on BOTH routes — link-in-emphasis.md paragraph 9 `[A bare link whose text begins with a space](essay.md) opens…` at the block's start: rendered `X[A bare…`, source `[XA bare…`; paragraph 7 `…see [the essay ](essay.md)` at the block's end: rendered `…](essay.md)X`, source `…[the essay X](essay.md)`. One invariant, and this task asserts it over the corpus with the instances as named guards on top (CLAUDE.md `## Code rules`): at a block's edge, where no inline boundary exists, the source caret is outside every enclosing mark the typed marks do not carry and inside every one they do — from the innermost mark outward, stopping at the first mark the typed marks carry (a nested `*foo **bar**` end with stored `[emphasis]`: after `**`, before `*`, `*foo **bar**X*`); an atom's and an inline-code run's own rule (`isLeafEnd`, 1.52/1.60) is unchanged and runs first for that leaf. The reconciliation's prototype — one loop over the entries enclosing the innermost leaf at the edge, comparing each mark entry's `node.type` with the typed marks' `type.name` (the schema's mark names equal the mdast node types: `emphasis`, `strong`, `delete`, `link`, `inline_code`) and answering the outermost left mark's range end (or start) — turned every member above green with toggle.test.ts and position-map-inverse.test.ts unchanged and exactly one pin red; it is the shape, not a mandate: read `innermostAt` (:317–330) and `delimiterPosition` (:531–558, the `toRendered` side, which already answers a closing delimiter with the position after the mark) before deciding. Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r8 N2 — Sol finding 2 should-fix Required; packages/editor/src/toggle.ts (`correspondences`, `walkInline`, `walkBlock` and the two directions' leaf arithmetic, the cursor map of passed tasks 1.7, 1.37, 1.43, 1.52, 1.53, 1.60 and 1.63) and packages/editor/src/schema.ts (`stripUnparsableWhitespace`, the conversion of passed tasks 1.1, 1.13, 1.29 and 1.30), whose records are not edited — a new task per DECISIONS #016): inline correspondences derive live ProseMirror positions from the normalised tree's widths, so every character after whitespace the conversion drops is mapped one place off, in both directions, and the inverse holds while both are wrong. The cause, read in the tree: `walkInline` (toggle.ts:164–178) starts at the block's content start and advances by `inlineWidth` of each mdast node (:135–150 — the value's length, a mark's children's sum, one for an atom); `stripUnparsableWhitespace` (schema.ts:905–940, called at :567, :573, :624 with `LINE_ENDING` or `CELL_LINE_ENDING`) has already dropped `LEADING_WHITESPACE` (:759) at a line start (except a block-initial link's), `TRAILING_WHITESPACE` (:760) at the block's end, collapsed every `LINE_ENDING_RUN` (:770) to one line ending, dropped runs that became empty and trailing `hard_break`s, while `unmarkEdgeWhitespace` moved edge whitespace out of marks — and the live document still holds every one of those characters. Reproduced headlessly by the reconciliation at 970bb5c: `a `+"`cd`"+` b`, the first character deleted, live text ` `+"`cd`"+` b` (the readout's `before: " c"`), caret between `c` and `d`: `toSource` answers column 3 — rendered `\`cXd\` b`, source `\`cdX\` b`; the same for plain text (`cXd b` vs `cdX b`), emphasis, strong and a list item; `toRendered(toSource(p)) === p` at every one (both directions share the false start). Over the corpus, the first character of every textblock deleted (248 blocks in the 65 fixtures): 54 blocks lose their lead, and at every text position of those blocks the two views disagree (4,374 of 4,374 positions checked in them); the six disagreements outside them are members of recorded classes (`[1.53]`'s before side on an astral neighbour, L9's autolink literal, and N1's link-edge members that 1.63 fixes). Sol's constraints, kept: the serializer's forbidden whitespace is not restored and the live buffer is not touched — the loss is decided (tasks 1.13/1.29/1.30); the correspondence is what is wrong. Do exactly this. (1) Export from packages/editor/src/schema.ts one function that performs `stripUnparsableWhitespace`'s normalisation AND returns, for every kept output node, the live position of each of its characters (a kept-character map: output offset → live position, plus the live range each output node covers) — and make `stripUnparsableWhitespace` a projection of it, so the two cannot disagree (one implementation of every branch: the line-start rule, the block-initial link exception, the line-ending run, the empty run, the block-end loop, the trailing break); its doc comment states the ownership rule for a live position that sits inside dropped whitespace ONCE (the position maps to the next kept character; at the block's end, to the block's end) — the rule tested at the first, middle and last dropped character (CLAUDE.md `## Code rules`). (2) `correspondences` in toggle.ts consumes it: `walkBlock` hands each textblock's ProseMirror inline children and its line ending to that function, and every inline correspondence's `pmStart`/`pmEnd` are live positions; the leaf-interior arithmetic — `pos - inside.pmStart` in `toSource` (:506, the spelling-table index) and `entry.pmStart + spellingIndex(…)` in `toRendered` (:522) — translates through the kept-character map in both directions, and `inlineWidth` is deleted or reduced to the atom case (say which in the journal). A document with no dropped whitespace has identical correspondences to today's — the guard that the change is a no-op there is the existing corpus inverse leg and toggle.test.ts's whole inverse family, green unchanged. (3) Guards in packages/editor/test/toggle.test.ts, one `describe` titled for the rule, enumerating whitespace classes — a lead at the block's start, a lead after a hard break, a trailing run at the block's end, a line-ending run with spaces on both sides (a paragraph's `LINE_ENDING` and a cell's `CELL_LINE_ENDING`), a whitespace-only run between two nodes, a dropped trailing hard break — × node classes — plain text, marked text, inline code, a link's text, a run beside an atom — × containers — paragraph, heading, list item, blockquote, table cell — with one astral member; each seeded from a typing-shaped or deleting transaction on `mdastToPM(parse(·))` (never a hand-built ProseMirror doc), asserting the two views' bytes by `toBe` at the positions on both sides of the dropped whitespace (`typedInRendered` against `typedInSource` on `format(pmToMdast(live))`), the inverse over every text position, and the dropped-whitespace ownership rule at its three positions. (4) The corpus leg `deleteAtEveryBlockStart` in packages/editor/test/position-map-inverse.test.ts beside the two destructive legs (the 30 s per-test timeout in 1.61's form and comment): for every fixture in the index, the first character of every textblock outside a fenced code block deleted, and at every text position of that block the two views' bytes equal AND the inverse holds — a third destructive transaction in the family (CLAUDE.md: a corpus leg seeded from the writing surface's own output includes a destructive transaction); the leg records how many blocks lost their lead and asserts at least one did and at least one did not (both sides of the clause; the reconciliation's sweep: 54 of 248 — a count read from the run, never a literal in the test); named exclusions positively bounded (DECISIONS #032): the `[1.53]` members (a raw source keystroke before or after a punctuation-edged run, the rendered bytes carrying `X`) and `[review-1-r6 L9]`'s member (a character typed inside an autolink literal's text, the rendered bytes a `[text](url)` link) — each excluded position asserted to be of its class, never `it.fails`, never a narrowing. (5) One Playwright spec, e2e/web/editor-toggle-stripped-lead.spec.ts, Sol's route: load `a `+"`cd`"+` b`, click at the left edge of the paragraph's first character measured from its text node's own `Range` rect (1.62's measured-click shape; an interior text position with one DOM spelling), poll the readout equal to `{ before: "", empty: true, marks: [], stored: null }`, press `Delete`, poll `before: ""` with the pane equal to `\`cd\` b

` by `toBe`, the fixed point; a second case the strong twin `a **cd** b` → `**cXd** b
`. No Home/End key, no `ControlOrMeta+` chord for the caret, no DOM selection read (DECISIONS #022, #024, #037). (6) Asserted able to fail, recorded in the journal and not committed: the width arithmetic restored in `walkInline` — the corpus leg red at the stripped-lead blocks and the (3) lead guards red (record the received columns). Pins: the reconciliation ran no prototype of this shape; the legs named in (2) assert positions of documents with no dropped whitespace, which the change leaves as they are — a pin that turns red is a defect of the implementation, not a pin to rewrite: stop, journal it with the position and both values, and do not edit the pin in this task. description: Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r8 N3 — Claude finding 1 should-fix; packages/core/src/format.ts, the per-child widening walk of passed task 1.57, and packages/core/src/positions.ts, `formatWithMap`'s `unresolved` of passed tasks 1.2, 1.46, 1.51 and 1.59, whose records are not edited — a new task per DECISIONS #016): the walk's give-up path is unguarded — `locateChild`'s `return undefined` (format.ts:431–432, the only uncovered line in the tree at the r8 gate, coverage lines 99.94 %) reached from `widenSplitSurrogateReferences` (:515, `if (located === undefined) break;`) silently leaves children i+1…n unwidened, and the doc comment (:500–503) discharges the branch by saying `locateEmission` in positions.ts enumerates the same forms so the map's corpus case guards it — false as written: `locateEmission` (positions.ts:635–652) finds a child with `container.indexOf(candidate.text, cursor)`, a forward search that succeeds at ANY offset at or after the cursor, and offers a non-text child one candidate, its raw handler value, while `locateChild` requires `joined.startsWith(form.text, cursor)` AT the cursor and carries head/tail-encoded and eol-as-space forms; the more permissive enumeration is the guard, so the corpus case stays green while the walk gives up. Reproduced by the reconciliation as unreachable today: with the `break` replaced by a throw, the whole unit suite at 970bb5c (44 files, 3,947 tests, every fixture, parse(fixture) and format(parse(·))) ran with zero throws; Claude's 11,560 swept trees plus the 65 corpus files against an instrumented counter: 0 give-ups. A missing guard, not a live defect — the class M2's promoted rule names (a rewrite the map cannot follow is one the parser cannot read), and Claude's risk 3: the two paths that resolve a surprise by doing less, quietly, this one and `applyEdits`' overlap skip (:475, `if (edit.start < at) continue`). Do exactly this. (1) The walk records its give-up per call, never in module-level state (CLAUDE.md `packages/core` rules: pure functions with injected state): read how `handleRoot` (:669–706) installs the recorder on the serializer's `state` for that `toMarkdown` call (`installSurrogateWidening`, :567–590) and record the give-up there — the parent's path or node and the index and type of the child the walk could not locate — or thread it back from the walk as a return value; `format` keeps today's bytes (the walk stops; nothing is widened blind). (2) `formatWithMap` (positions.ts:194) reports each recorded give-up as an `unresolved` entry (the map's existing instrument, a path string naming the parent and the child index; the `PositionMap` doc comment at :34–40 updated) — read `formatWithMap` first to confirm the widening walk runs under it as it does under `format` (the same extension list from :701); if it does not, make it so and say so in the journal. The corpus case "maps every node of the tree, and nothing is unresolved" (packages/core/test/positions-corpus.test.ts) then covers the walk for every fixture; confirm it also runs over `format(parse(·))` of each fixture (Claude's second leg) and, if it does not, add that leg beside it. (3) A hand-built guard that reaches the branch: export the walk (or a thin test-only entry) and call it with a `RecordedChild` whose value is absent from the join — the give-up recorded, the join returned unchanged, the children before it widened and the ones after it untouched (the walk's contract stated in its doc comment) — so format.ts:432 is covered by a test that asserts the behaviour, not by a mutation alone. (4) The same treatment for `applyEdits`' overlap skip (:475): either an overlapping edit is recorded the same way and reported through `unresolved`, or one paragraph in the journal names why two edits cannot overlap by construction and the test that shows it — decide from the code, record the decision in the doc comment. (5) The doc comment at :495–503 rewritten: the instrument (`unresolved`) is the guard; the sentence naming `locateEmission` as the equivalent enumeration deleted; the two enumerations' difference (`indexOf` vs `startsWith`, the candidate sets) stated in one sentence so the next reader does not rebuild the false argument. description: Shell e2e input routes on the embedded WebDriver provider, repair 2 of the 2.verifyh GATE-FAILED at a1 (ci.yml run 36292723305 at 5c086c6, ref ci/2.verify/a1; evidence /logs/ci/2.verifyh/a1/e2e-shell/). The embedded provider (tauri-plugin-wdio-webdriver, used on windows and macOS) makes every input synthetic JS: printable keys append to an input's value ignoring its selection and do nothing in a contenteditable, and pointer actions dispatch untrusted MouseEvents that place no caret; its execute/sync polls a window result variable that location.reload() wipes. Symptoms: windows — autosave, file-tree, images and robustness fail in "before all" at `browser.execute(() => location.reload())` (30 s script timeout, then the 60 s hook timeout), and file-tree reads 'a.mdb.md' !== 'b.md' after F2 rename; macOS (recorded) — typed text never reaches the document ('Hello\n' where 'HelloX\n' is expected) and the same rename result. Ubuntu (external tauri-driver) is 6/6 green and its routes stay unchanged. Add e2e/shell/test/routes.ts, keyed on selectDriverProvider(platform(), process.env.ESSAYDOWN_E2E_DRIVER) (never process.platform in a spec): on the embedded branch a reload is browser.refresh() (never location.reload(), and not reloadSession() right after a fresh localStorage write), the caret is placed at a block's end with Range.selectNodeContents(block).collapse(false) + Selection.addRange + the editor's focus() via execute, typing is $(editor).addValue(text), and a rename field is set with $(input).setValue(name); F2/Enter/Escape and clickCentreOf stay. Use the routes in autosave, file-tree, images and robustness specs. The container reproduces the embedded leg with ESSAYDOWN_E2E_DRIVER=embedded under Xvfb (lesson [2.1.g1]); run each leg as one foreground call bounded by `timeout`, never in the background. If WebView2 also hangs on refresh() at the gate, the next planning commit chooses the route; this task does not.
acceptance: Every spec under e2e/shell/test/ passes in the container on both legs — the default external tauri-driver leg and ESSAYDOWN_E2E_DRIVER=embedded — with both commands and their spec totals recorded in the journal; `grep -c 'location.reload' e2e/shell/test/*.ts` prints 0 for every file and no spec reads process.platform; one guard per embedded route (reload, caret-to-end, typing, rename) with its mutation recorded in the journal (the route reverted, the spec red, and the failure quoted); no dependency-manifest or lockfile change; scripts/check green. The journal states that on the embedded provider every event is synthetic, so the embedded leg proves DOM → ProseMirror → store → disk and only the external leg proves native input.

description: Windows rename rollback test and assets/sidecar collision guard, repair 1 of the 2.verify.g2h GATE-FAILED at a1 (RUNNER-SPEC §2 rewrite rule (a); ci.yml run 36324256194 at 40c9be2, ref ci/2.verify.g2/a1; evidence /logs/ci/2.verify.g2h/a1/). Every job is green except `test (windows-latest)` → Cargo test: 55 tests, 54 pass, one fails: `workspace::tests::rename_rolls_back_doc_and_sidecar_when_moving_assets_fails` panics at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/workspace.rs:902 `assertion failed: result.is_err()` (test-logs/test-logs-windows-latest/cargo-test.log lines 663–685); Linux and macOS pass it. Cause: the test injects the failure by placing a plain FILE at `assets/b` and expecting `std::fs::rename(assets/a, assets/b)` to fail. On Unix that is `rename(2)` directory-over-file = ENOTDIR. On Windows, Rust 1.98.1 `std::fs::rename` (library/std/src/sys/fs/windows.rs `pub fn rename`) calls `MoveFileExW(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)` and on ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED retries through `SetFileInformationByHandle(FileRenameInfoEx)` with `FILE_RENAME_FLAG_REPLACE_IF_EXISTS | FILE_RENAME_FLAG_POSIX_SEMANTICS`; the NT rename rules refuse a replace only when the target is a directory, read-only or executing, so a directory source replaces a plain file and the rename succeeds — the injection never fires, and in production a user file sitting at `assets/<newstem>` is silently destroyed on Windows (an empty directory there is silently swallowed on every OS; an existing `<newstem>.essaydown.json` is silently overwritten on every OS by the file→file rename). Fix, two parts, in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/workspace.rs only. (1) `rename_file_at`: resolve `new_sidecar` and `new_assets` before the existing `new_doc.exists()` check and return `Err(WorkspaceError::Io(io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists))` when any of `new_doc`, `new_sidecar`, `new_assets` exists, before the first `std::fs::rename`; update the fn doc comment to say the target document, sidecar or assets directory already existing is `AlreadyExists` and changes nothing. Rollback logic is unchanged. (2) Tests in `mod tests`: (a) add `rename_onto_an_existing_assets_file_is_already_exists_and_changes_nothing` — a.md with `![x](assets/a/x.png)`, sidecar, `assets/a/x.png` = "img", plain file `assets/b` = "blocker"; asserts `matches!(err, WorkspaceError::Io(io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists))`, a.md and a.essaydown.json byte-unchanged, b.md and b.essaydown.json absent, `assets/a/x.png` reads "img", `assets/b` reads "blocker". (b) add `rename_onto_an_existing_empty_assets_dir_is_already_exists_and_changes_nothing` — same setup with an empty directory `assets/b` instead; same assertions plus `assets/b` still a directory (the case POSIX rename would otherwise swallow). (c) add `rename_onto_an_existing_sidecar_is_already_exists_and_changes_nothing` — a.md, a.essaydown.json = `{"version":1}`, pre-existing b.essaydown.json = `{"version":2}`; asserts AlreadyExists, a.md present, b.md absent, both sidecars byte-unchanged. (d) rewrite `rename_rolls_back_doc_and_sidecar_when_moving_assets_fails`: setup a.md `![x](assets/a/x.png)`, sidecar `{"version":1}`, `assets/a/x.png` = "img", NO `assets/b`; injection before the call: `#[cfg(unix)]` set `assets` to `Permissions::from_mode(0o555)` (twin of `write_doc_to_permission_denied_dir_returns_permission_denied`), `#[cfg(windows)]` `let held = std::fs::File::open(root.join("assets").join("a").join("x.png")).unwrap();` kept alive across the call (FILE_RENAME_INFORMATION rules: a directory cannot be renamed while any file beneath it has an open handle; MoveFileExW reports ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED and std's FileRenameInfoEx fallback returns that same error); after the call, `#[cfg(unix)]` restore 0o755 and `#[cfg(windows)]` `drop(held)` before any assertion; then assert `matches!(err, WorkspaceError::Io(io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied))` (replacing `result.is_err()`), a.md and a.essaydown.json byte-unchanged, b.md and b.essaydown.json absent, `assets/a/x.png` reads "img", `assets/b` absent. Do not gate the test itself with `#[cfg(unix)]`; only the injection and its cleanup are cfg-gated. Zero new dependencies; nothing else changes.
acceptance: `git diff --name-only "$(git merge-base HEAD phase/2)" HEAD` lists only apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/workspace.rs, docs/progress/journal-main.md and docs/lessons.md. In `rename_file_at` the three `.exists()` checks on `new_doc`, `new_sidecar` and `new_assets` all precede the first `std::fs::rename` (line numbers from `grep -n`, quoted in the journal). `cargo test -- --list` lists `rename_onto_an_existing_assets_file_is_already_exists_and_changes_nothing`, `rename_onto_an_existing_empty_assets_dir_is_already_exists_and_changes_nothing`, `rename_onto_an_existing_sidecar_is_already_exists_and_changes_nothing` and `rename_rolls_back_doc_and_sidecar_when_moving_assets_fails` on Linux (no `#[cfg(unix)]`/`#[cfg(windows)]` attribute on any of the four `#[test]` fns; `grep -c '#\[cfg(windows)\]' apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/workspace.rs` grew by exactly 2 and `#\[cfg(unix)\]` by exactly 2, all four inside the rollback test body). The rollback test asserts `io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied` and contains no `is_err()`; its assertions on a.md, a.essaydown.json, b.md and b.essaydown.json are unchanged from 40c9be2. Removing the production guard alone makes tests (a) and (c) fail on Linux — remove it in the working tree (save it first with `git diff > ` a file under /tmp and `git apply -R`, never `git stash`, whose stack is shared across worktrees), run, record both failing test names in the journal, restore with `git apply`, confirm `git diff` is back. scripts/check green. The journal quotes the failing cargo-test.log line (`assertion failed: result.is_err()` at workspace.rs:902), names the std path (`MoveFileExW(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)` then `FileRenameInfoEx` with `REPLACE_IF_EXISTS|POSIX_SEMANTICS`, library/std/src/sys/fs/windows.rs) as why a directory replaced a plain file on Windows, names which test discharges each guard clause (doc: the existing `rename_onto_an_existing_target_is_already_exists_and_changes_nothing`; sidecar: (c); assets: (a) and (b)) and which injection discharges rollback per OS, and states that only the `test (windows-latest)` leg of the 2.verify.g3h CI gate proves the Windows injection: `rename_rolls_back_doc_and_sidecar_when_moving_assets_fails ... ok` in test-logs-windows-latest/cargo-test.log with 0 failures. If that leg instead reports another kind or Ok, the next repair swaps the `#[cfg(windows)]` injection to the existing icacls helpers `deny_write_access(&root.join("assets"))`/`allow_write_access` and never weakens the rollback assertions.

description: Phase 2 review fix, save lifecycle (DECISIONS #review-2-r0 U1, U6, U20 — Sol r0 finding 1 blocker, Claude r0 finding 1 blocker, Claude 4 should-fix Required, Claude 15; taken under Michael's stop rule DECISIONS #041 D1 and his approval of the r0 list; files of passed tasks 2.4 and 2.5, whose records are not edited — a new task per DECISIONS #016). Scope: apps/desktop/src/workspace/document-sync.ts, apps/desktop/src/workspace/DocumentPane.tsx, apps/desktop/src/App.tsx, tests/document-sync.test.ts, e2e/shell/test/autosave.spec.ts, e2e/shell/test/file-tree.spec.ts, docs/lessons.md, the journal. Defect: type into a document, let another writer change the file (the 'Changed on disk' banner appears), then click any other tree entry, Open Folder… or rename the open file — the typed text is gone from memory and disk with no message (Sol's native probe at 01a4c72: before `Alpha.LOCAL`, after and on disk `EXTERNAL.`); a failed `write_doc` followed by a switch loses the text the same way and `setError(null)` erases the failure. Cause: `flush()` (document-sync.ts:225-229 at 01a4c72) resolves alike when it saved, skipped on conflict, or failed (`save()` routes a write error to `failed()` and resolves, :129-132), and the three callers (App.tsx:99 `openFile`, :150 `openFolderDialog`, :176 `commitRename`) read resolved as saved and remount, whose cleanup `sync.dispose()` (DocumentPane.tsx:165) drops the buffer. Beside it: `save()` clears `dirty` only after the write lands (:134) while `known` moves before it (:126), so a `flush()` during an in-flight write re-reads pre-write bytes and raises a spurious conflict; DocumentPane.tsx:124 reads `{root, sidecar}` after `await write_doc`, so doc and sidecar can come from different snapshots; a renamed open document keeps its old `known` and store (App.tsx:180-181; DocumentPane.tsx:157 drops the new path's reports), so the next save after a rename that rewrote image URLs sees disk ≠ known and raises a false 'Changed on disk', where Keep mine writes the stale URLs back. Fix: (1) `flush(): Promise<"clean" | "saved" | "conflict" | "failed">`, resolving only after any in-flight write; one in-flight promise in the closure that `save()`, `keepMine()` and `flush()` await and `check()` defers behind; the serialised bytes and the sidecar snapshot read in one synchronous step before the first `await` (the rule stated once in the module doc comment). (2) `openFile`, `openFolderDialog`, `commitRename` proceed only on `clean` or `saved`; otherwise the pane, its banner and the error stay (no `setError(null)`) and one line on the existing error surface says the switch waits for the banner's choice — no new dialog, no third button. (3) After `rename_file` resolves for the open document, the pane re-reads the new path: bytes equal to `known` → nothing (undo history kept); different → the path an external change to a clean document takes (`reloaded`), never a conflict. Guards, one test each (vitest in tests/document-sync.test.ts): flush during a conflict → `conflict`, dirty kept, no write; flush after a failed write → `failed`, dirty kept; flush while a write is in flight → awaits it, no second read, no conflict, `saved`; a watcher report during an in-flight write is deferred and the write's own echo reads as ours; flush when clean → `clean`, no write; keepMine during an in-flight write awaits it. e2e, run one spec at a time in the container as one foreground call bounded by `timeout` (never `run_in_background` or a wakeup): `timeout 900 sh -c 'Xvfb :99 -ac & DISPLAY=:99 pnpm --filter @essaydown/e2e-shell test -- --spec <file>'` (lesson [2.1.g1]'s substitute for `xvfb-run`; lesson [2.5]'s `clickCentreOf` route, never `$().click()`); the embedded leg and the three OSes are proven by the 2.verify.r1h CI gate: autosave.spec.ts — dirty + external append → banner → click the b.md tree entry → `current-file` still a.md, the editor's text still holds the typed character, disk unchanged; then Keep mine → the switch succeeds; file-tree.spec.ts — after renaming the open document, type one character, wait past the debounce, b.md on disk holds it and no `conflict-banner` exists. The write-failure route is the vitest guard (an OS-level injection differs per runner; the journal says so — no `.skip`). No Home/End key or modifier chord in any e2e, byte-exact text through `textContent` and `assert.equal` (lesson [2.4]), no magnitude from one run asserted (CLAUDE.md).

description: Phase 2 test-only repair 1 of the 2.verify.r1h GATE-FAILED at a1 (RUNNER-SPEC §2 rewrite rule (a); ci.yml run 36690847581 at fbce99e, ref ci/2.verify.r1/a1; evidence /logs/ci/2.verify.r1h/a1/). Four test-side defects; no product change. The failing assertions were all added by 2.17–2.20 and first ran on macOS and Windows at this gate; the same file-tree cases were green on all three OSes at 2.verify.g3h. (a) `test (windows-latest)`: `workspace::tests::new_file_on_u64_max_existing_name_is_io_error_not_panic` panics in its own setup at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/workspace.rs:956 (`Os { code: 123, kind: InvalidFilename }`) because it writes its fixture through `format!("{}/Untitled-{}.md", root.display(), u64::MAX)`; `scratch_dir()` canonicalises, a canonical Windows root is a verbatim `\\?\` path, and a verbatim path treats `/` as a name character. The product path is unaffected (`new_file_at` resolves every candidate through `resolve_workspace_path` → `root.join`). Fix: build the fixture path with `root.join(format!("Untitled-{}.md", u64::MAX))`; the assertion is unchanged. (b) `e2e-shell` macOS and Windows, e2e/shell/test/file-tree.spec.ts "clicking a cloudOnly entry shows the tooltip and does not error" fails at its `[data-testid="error"]` absence check: the spec's `before()` seeds `a.essaydown.json` as `{"sentences":[]}`, which `sidecarSchema` (packages/core/src/sidecar.ts) rejects; since 2.19 the first save re-reads the sidecar, `chooseSidecarForWrite` (apps/desktop/src/workspace/sidecar-sync.ts) skips the unparseable file and the pane reports it through the error banner. On Linux's external provider `reloadSession()` is a process restart that clears the banner before the cloudOnly case; on the embedded provider (macOS, Windows, and the container's embedded leg) it re-creates the session inside the running process, so the banner persists. Before fixing, read `[data-testid="error"]`'s `textContent` once on the embedded leg and record it in the journal. Fix: seed a valid sidecar (the shape `emptySidecar()` serialises, `version` 1); in the test "after renaming the open document, a typed character saves to b.md without a conflict" also assert `[data-testid="error"]` absent after the save; and state in the comment on the spec's relaunch helper that on the embedded provider `reloadSession()` re-creates the session inside the running process and is a process restart only on the external provider. (c) `e2e-shell (windows-latest)`, file-tree.spec.ts "renames a.md to b.md via F2, moving the sidecar and assets together": the image-src assertion (`decodeURIComponent(src).includes("assets/b/image.png")`) encodes the POSIX separator; the Windows src decodes to a `\\?\C:\…\assets\b\image.png` path (e2e-shell-windows-latest/e2e-shell.log around line 5048) while the image loaded. (d) `e2e-shell` macOS and Windows, e2e/shell/test/close.spec.ts `FAILED in undefined`: on the embedded provider the WebDriver server lives in the app process, so after the close-requested barrier destroys the last window the app exits and the relaunch read-back's `browser.reloadSession()` gets ECONNREFUSED/ECONNRESET. Fix: run the relaunch read-back only when `selectDriverProvider(platform(), process.env.ESSAYDOWN_E2E_DRIVER)` (e2e/shell/provider.ts, the switch wdio.conf.ts already reads) is `"external"`, with a comment naming why; the embedded leg ends at the on-disk byte assertion, which is unchanged — a capability branch, never `.skip()`. description: Phase 2 review fix, macOS menu Quit goes through the close barrier (DECISIONS #review-2-r1 U2 — Claude r1 finding 2 blocker, Sol r1 finding 2 blocker; the quit half of #review-2-r0 U2, which 2.17 handed to the principal, lesson [2.17] (2); taken under DECISIONS #041 D1 and Michael's approval). Scope: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs, a new apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/menu.rs with its `#[cfg(test)]` module, docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md (one line), docs/lessons.md, the journal. No frontend change: the barrier is App.tsx:100-126 and `decideClose` (2.17). Defect (source-confirmed, not run on macOS): `Builder::default()` installs tauri's default menu on macOS (tauri 2.11.5 src/app.rs:2245-2247) whose Quit is `PredefinedMenuItem::quit` (src/menu/menu.rs:194); muda 0.19.3 maps it to `terminate:` (src/platform_impl/macos/mod.rs:994); tao 0.35.3 implements no `applicationShouldTerminate:` (src/platform_impl/macos/app_delegate.rs:63,131), so Cmd+Q raises neither CloseRequested nor ExitRequested, and keystrokes inside the 500 ms debounce, or edits held by 'Changed on disk' or a failed write, are lost silently. Fix: first read the installed tauri's `Menu::default` (menu.rs; quote the line range in the journal) and derive from its branches a pure `fn default_menu_spec() -> Vec<SubmenuSpec>` (an enum per entry: `Predefined(kind)` or `Custom { id, text, accelerator }`) that mirrors every submenu and item the default builds on macOS — the app submenu, File, Edit (its predefined undo/redo/cut/copy/paste/select_all are the selectors the webview's Cmd+Z/X/C/V/A run through, so a menu without them breaks editing silently), View, Window, Help as present — except that the app submenu's Quit is `Custom { id: "quit", text: "Quit Essay Down", accelerator: "CmdOrCtrl+Q" }` at the same position; a `build_menu(handle, spec)` maps the spec to `tauri::menu` items; the builder installs it with `Builder::menu` under `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` only (Linux and Windows keep no menu bar, as today) and registers `on_menu_event` whose `quit` arm calls `fn request_quit(app)`: for every `app.webview_windows()` value call `close()`, raising CloseRequested so the JS barrier flushes and destroys, the app exiting with its last window; a `close()` error is logged with the window label and the app keeps running (CLAUDE.md: a checked outcome, never alike on success and failure). No `RunEvent::ExitRequested` handler (it is never raised on this route, lesson [2.17]); no new IPC command (PRD §6.4); no capability change; zero new crates (`tauri::menu` is the `tauri` crate, PRD §4). Correct `lib.rs`'s plugin comment while editing it (`[review-2-r0 U29]`'s trigger: the first task that edits `lib.rs`). Guards (cargo, in menu.rs's test module, enumerated from the diff): (1) `default_menu_spec()` contains no `Predefined(Quit)`; (2) exactly one `Custom` item, id `quit`, accelerator `CmdOrCtrl+Q`, in the first submenu at the default's Quit position; (3) every predefined kind of the installed default's macOS branch is present once — the kind table typed from menu.rs's branches with the line range in the journal, with an absence case (a spec missing `Paste` fails the comparison); (4) the dispatch `fn quit_requested(id: &MenuId) -> bool` true for `quit`, false for any other id; (5) if `tauri::test::mock_builder()` can build the spec (read `tauri::menu` and `tauri::test` under MockRuntime first; record the reading), `build_menu` over the spec yields a menu whose item count per submenu equals the spec's — if it cannot, record why and guards (1)-(4) stand alone. The macOS behaviour is recorded, not claimed (the container is Linux); the three-OS build and cargo run are proven by the 2.verify.r2 CI gate, and the Cmd+Q route by Michael at human gate 2.25. Append one docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md line `[review-2-r1, U2 terminate: routes]`: Dock → Quit, logout and shutdown send `terminate:` with no menu item in the path and tao 0.35.3 turns `applicationWillTerminate` into an unpreventable exit; revisit when a tao or tauri release exposes `applicationShouldTerminate:` (an ExitRequested raised for it), and at the Phase 6 packaging human gate, which performs a Dock-Quit check inside the debounce and records the outcome; hard stop `6.verify`. First, before any read of node_modules: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. `node ralph/journal.mjs stub 2.24` before implementing; each attempt appends its own journal line. Record every compiler-forced decision in the commit body (CLAUDE.md).

description: Phase 2 review fix, a barrier result covers the latest edit and a rename's rewrite reaches a dirty editor (DECISIONS #review-2-r2 W1, W2 — Sol r2 findings 1 and 2, both blocker; Claude r2's D1 scope confirmed r1's fixes only and did not read this module; taken under DECISIONS #041 D1 and Michael's approval; files of passed tasks 2.16–2.18 and 2.20, whose records are not edited — a new task per DECISIONS #016). Scope: apps/desktop/src/workspace/document-sync.ts, apps/desktop/src/workspace/DocumentPane.tsx (the rename effect only), tests/document-sync.test.ts, docs/lessons.md, the journal. No change to App.tsx, packages/core, any Rust file, any e2e, manifest, lockfile or capability; zero new dependencies (PRD §4). Read Sol's reproduction first: /logs/reviews/2/r2/sol/probes.mjs and probes.log (injected I/O with held write promises against the transpiled unchanged module; no native timing claim). W1 defect: `write()` (document-sync.ts:171-186) captures `at = generation`, leaves `dirty` true when an `edited()` lands during `await io.write`, but returns `saved` regardless; `flush()` (:285-293) returns that result, and App.tsx's close handler destroys the window on it (`decideClose`), `openFile` replaces the pane on it, and the rename handler proceeds on it — the later keystroke is never written (probes.log:1 `result:"saved", dirty:true`, disk `first edit\n`, editor `first edit plus later keystroke\n`). The autosave timer path keeps its current behaviour (its next timer writes the newer edit). W2 defect: `renamed()` (:294-311) adopts the rewritten disk bytes as `known` but keeps a dirty editor that still holds `assets/<old stem>/`; the next save passes `disk === known` and writes the old URLs over the moved assets, so the image is broken on reopen (probes.log:2); tests/document-sync.test.ts's "rewritten bytes under an edit move known without a reload or a conflict" enshrines it with abstract strings. W2 fix: `renamed(rewrite: (text: string) => string)` — DocumentPane's rename effect passes `(text) => rewriteAssetUrls(text, stemOf(old path), stemOf(new path))` (`pathSeen.current` before it is overwritten is the old path; `rewriteAssetUrls` is @essaydown/core's, `stemOf` is ./paths); when the document is dirty after adoption, the sync hands the editor `rewrite(serialize())` through the existing `reloaded` callback and stays dirty, so the edit is kept and the next save writes it with the new stem; a clean document reloads the disk bytes as today; equal stems are `rewriteAssetUrls`'s identity (its corpus identity leg exists in packages/core/test/rewrite-asset-urls.test.ts and is not touched). Then port `apps/desktop/src/dev/DevEditor.tsx`'s toggle into `apps/desktop/src/workspace/DocumentPane.tsx`: a `surface` of `rendered | source` beside `mode`, one of the two views mounted over the pane's one store; `togglePlugins(toggle)` in the ProseMirror plugins; the source view built from `format(root)` with `sourceExtensions()`, `sourceToggleKeymap(toggle)`, `sourceUndoKeymap(store, () => binding?.flush())`, an update listener into `bindCodeMirror`, and `destroy()` on unmount; `toggle` flushes the binding, carries the caret through `cursorMap(...).toSource(head, storedMarks)` or `canonicalCursor(text, sourceCursor(state))`, then `toggleMode`; the incoming view places it through `toRendered`/`renderedSelection` or `sourceOffset` and focuses. DOM contract for 3.20: the pane root (`data-testid="document"`) carries `data-surface`; in source only `[data-testid="source"] .cm-content` exists and no `.ProseMirror`; in rendered only `[data-testid="editor"] .ProseMirror` and no `[data-testid="source"]`; no button is added (§146 is the chord). The source host takes the rendered host's layout rules (Produce's 68ch). The toggle works in every §6.3 mode and forces none; mode panels keep reading `store.cursor`, which the source view does not drive — the journal and commit body record the cut (Michael's OK, DECISIONS #054) and this task appends the backlog line `[3.19, source caret does not drive the mode panels]` with hard stop the Phase 3→4 boundary planning, whose text says that in the source view a Rewrite or Reorder panel action acts on the last rich-view cursor with no visible cue, and that the fix candidate is a cue on the panel (greyed out, or labelled as following the rich-view cursor) while `data-surface` is `source`. Settling (CLAUDE.md stale-read rule), one seam (Michael's OK, DECISIONS #054): `packages/editor/src/store.ts` gains `settle()` on the state, a no-op until `bindCodeMirror` registers its `flush` (cleared on destroy), and `dispatch`, `undo` and `redo` call it first; the pane's `flush()` and `rename()` and `workspace/test-hook.ts`'s readers call `settle()` before they read; `DevEditor.tsx` is unchanged. Every typed string in the spec has no two identical consecutive characters (WebKitWebDriver drops the second; 3.6's spec comment) and is letters only. The chord is sent only through `routes.ts`'s `pressModChord("/")`; never a Home/End key or a caret chord (DECISIONS #022). Run every e2e spec as one foreground call per CLAUDE.md's long-command rule (DECISIONS #049); e2e/web runs because store.ts changes (lesson `[3.4]`).
acceptance: Headless (`packages/editor/test/toggle.test.ts`): with a source change pending inside the window, `dispatch`, `undo` and `redo` each settle it first (the committed snapshot holds the typed text and the mutation on top; the undo steps back over the burst, never drops it); `settle` is a no-op with no binding and after destroy. WebdriverIO `e2e/shell/test/source-toggle.spec.ts` on a fixture-seeded workspace, in the container (Linux): (1) Cmd/Ctrl+/ from the rendered view shows `[data-testid="source"] .cm-content` whose `.cm-line` join equals `format(parse(file))` byte-exact and no `.ProseMirror`; Cmd/Ctrl+/ again restores `.ProseMirror`; `__essaydown.markdown()`, the file on disk and `snapshots()` are unchanged by the pair; (2) the caret placed by `caretAtText` at a known offset of a known paragraph lands in the source view on that paragraph's line (located by text, line number from index.json's `paragraphStartLines`) at that `ch`, and toggling back returns `__essaydown.cursor()` to the position before; (3) text typed in the source view, toggled back with no wait, shows in the rendered view, in `markdown()` and on disk, and still does after 1.5 s; (4) text typed in the source view followed at once by a switch to another file is on the first file's disk (the pane's `flush` settled it); (5) text typed in the source view followed at once by `__essaydown.dispatch(moveBlock(...))` leaves `markdown()` holding both the text and the move; (6) Cmd/Ctrl+1–4 then a toggle pair in each mode leaves the mode and `markdown()` unchanged and shows the source view in every mode; every chord in the spec is `pressModChord`. e2e/shell and e2e/web green in the container; `git diff --name-only "$(git merge-base HEAD phase/3)" HEAD` lists only apps/desktop/src/workspace/DocumentPane.tsx, apps/desktop/src/workspace/test-hook.ts, apps/desktop/src/App.css, packages/editor/src/store.ts, packages/editor/src/toggle.ts, packages/editor/test/toggle.test.ts, e2e/shell/test/routes.ts, e2e/shell/test/source-toggle.spec.ts, docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md, docs/lessons.md and docs/progress/journal-main.md; the journal names the test that discharges each guard; zero new dependencies; suite green.
