description: Phase 3 test-only repair 1 of the 3.verifyh GATE-FAILED at a1 (RUNNER-SPEC §2 rewrite rule (a); ci.yml run 37423998582 at f897498, ref ci/3.verify/a1; evidence /logs/ci/3.verifyh/a1/e2e-shell/). ubuntu 15/15; macOS 10/15 (required, DECISIONS #047); Windows 13/15 (recorded). Three route defects in e2e/shell/test/routes.ts on the embedded provider (tauri-plugin-wdio-webdriver 1.4.0, the leg macOS and Windows drive, e2e/shell/provider.ts); no product change — RewritePanel.tsx:218–219 and reveal.ts:176–183 behave as specified under native input, which only the Linux leg sends. The Phase 3 shell specs ran in the container on the external leg only (journal [3.4]: 'embedded leg routes written, not run here'), so the gate was their first embedded run. (a) `pressModChord("Enter")` (routes.ts:314–316) is `browser.keys([MOD_KEY, "Enter"])`; the plugin's `dispatch_key_event` (src/platform/executor.rs:1216–1405 of the 1.4.0 crate — read it from the crate source, `cargo` registry or static.crates.io, never from memory) builds the KeyboardEvent for Enter, Escape, Space, Tab, Backspace, Delete, the arrows and the F-keys with no metaKey/ctrlKey/shiftKey/altKey; only `dispatch_regular_key` (printable characters) carries ModifierState — so `isModEnter` sees a bare Enter: rewrite.spec.ts 'add 2 variants…' (`addVariant` :167; macOS log 93–96, Windows 74–79) and one-workflow step 4 (:350), the later rewrite cases cascading. Fix, in `pressModChord` only: on the embedded leg a key WebdriverIO maps to a WebDriver named key (`key.length > 1`) is dispatched by one `browser.execute` as a `keydown` then a `keyup` KeyboardEvent on `document.activeElement` with `key`/`code` (`Enter`), `keyCode`/`which` 13, bubbles, cancelable, `metaKey: MOD_KEY === "Meta"`, `ctrlKey: MOD_KEY === "Control"`, shiftKey/altKey false — the provider's own synthetic route for printable chords; printable keys and the external leg keep `browser.keys`. (b) `selectDomText`'s `locate` (routes.ts:190–198) and `textPoint` (:152–169) walk every text node of a block, and the specs read offsets from `textContent` (one-workflow.spec.ts:308, :332–336; rewrite.spec.ts:135–139, :284, :315–325; reorder.spec.ts:150), but the reveal plugin (packages/editor/src/reveal.ts:176–183, DECISIONS #037) draws the caret block's heading marker and mark delimiters as `contenteditable="false"` widget text inside the block the moment the caret enters it — `## ` is three characters. On the embedded leg the route sets the range, ProseMirror reveals the block, the next poll re-locates the offset over the longer node list and re-applies it three characters early, and the held check passes there: one-workflow step 3 split heading 1 at 26 of 29 on both OSes (`## What changed with metal ni` … `page.bs?`, macOS 31–57, Windows 36–63; 'producing under heading 1 never matched', :315); heading 0 survived only because the caret was already in it when its length was read. Fix: one ownership rule, stated once in routes.ts — a block's plain-text coordinate is the concatenation of its text nodes with no `[contenteditable="false"]` ancestor inside the block — applied by `textPoint`, by `locate`, and by an exported `editableTextOf(blockSelector)` the specs use for every length and `indexOf` read named above (no `textContent` offset or length read of an editor block remains in one-workflow, rewrite or reorder; rewrite's :317–319 comment restated to the rule); in-page helpers stay anonymous (reorder.spec.ts:108's `__name` note). Both halves move together: a walker that skips widgets with a spec that still reads `textContent` turns heading 0 red. (c) `reloadPage` (routes.ts:26–31) returns before the old document is gone: the plugin's refresh is `window.location.reload(); null;` (executor.rs:331–334), returning at once, so a readiness predicate already true on the stale document — the same file restored twice (outline.spec.ts:250 after :88–104; reorder.spec.ts:246 after :123–144; autosave.spec.ts:226 after :53–65) — passes, and the next command runs on the new document mid-load (outline 'delete the sidecar and reopen' `[]`, macOS 60–81; reorder keyboard case `[data-testid="mode-reorder"] is not on the page`, 86–90) or its execute result dies with the old window (autosave CRLF, bare `Error: Timeout`, 6–7; the race routes.ts:15–16 names; lesson [2.12]: WebKitGTK wins it, so the container cannot show it). Fix, embedded leg only: stamp the old document in one execute before the refresh (an attribute on `document.documentElement`), refresh, then poll `browser.getPageSource()` — the plugin's direct evaluate (executor.rs:341–352), not one of the six commands `@wdio/tauri-service` hooks (lesson [2.4]; `getTitle` is one), never an `execute` — until the stamp is absent, bounded at 15 s; the external leg is unchanged. If a lost page-source read proves to cost the script timeout at the gate, the fallback is `browser.setTimeout({ script: 1000 })` around the poll, restored after — the journal records which route stands. Guards in e2e/shell/test/routes.spec.ts, one per defect, enumerated from the diff: (a) a `keydown` listener installed by execute records {key, metaKey, ctrlKey}; `pressModChord("Enter")` yields key `Enter` with the platform's modifier true and the other false, on both legs; mutation: the branch reverted to `browser.keys` is red on the embedded leg in the container. (b) a heading (`# Hello`) with the caret first in another block: `caretAtText` at `editableTextOf`'s length then `typeText("X")` gives `# HelloX\n` byte-exact in `__essaydown.markdown()`; `editableTextOf` equals the heading's text while `textContent` holds the revealed marker (presence), and equals `textContent` on a paragraph with no marks (absence); mutation: the walker reverted to every text node is red on the embedded leg. (c) the existing reload guard (routes.spec.ts:56–86) is rewritten, never deleted: marker on the old document, readiness already true before the reload (the same file restored), `reloadPage()`, and the first execute after it returns reads the marker absent with no `waitFor`; its mutation (the poll removed) is recorded honestly as not reproducible in the container ([2.12]) and proved by the macOS e2e-shell leg of 3.verify.g1h. Before any fix, reproduce (a) and (b) in the container on the embedded leg — `ESSAYDOWN_E2E_DRIVER=embedded` under lesson [2.1.g1]'s `Xvfb :99 -ac` substitute — with one-workflow.spec.ts and rewrite.spec.ts, and quote each first error in the journal beside the gate's; if either does not reproduce, stop and journal the reading rather than guessing a fix. Then run the full e2e/shell suite on both legs as one foreground call per leg bounded by `timeout 540` (tool timeout 600000, output to a file then grepped; DECISIONS #049), as 3.20 did; a leg that does not finish inside the bound is run one spec file per call; then `scripts/check`. Append to docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md: `[3.21, embedded chords on named keys]` tauri-plugin-wdio-webdriver 1.4.0's named-key events carry no modifiers, so `pressModChord` synthesises them on the embedded leg; revisit when the pinned plugin's `dispatch_key_event` carries ModifierState (the branch goes, the guard stays); hard stop `4.verify`. Append a lessons line: a shell spec's embedded leg is run in the container before its task ends, because the gate is otherwise its first run. Scope: e2e/shell/test/routes.ts, routes.spec.ts, one-workflow.spec.ts, rewrite.spec.ts, reorder.spec.ts, docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md, docs/lessons.md, the journal; nothing under apps/ or packages/; no `.skip()`; no `process.platform` in a spec; no Home/End key or caret chord (DECISIONS #022); no magnitude from one run asserted (#024, #039); zero new dependencies and no plugin version change. First, before any read of node_modules: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. `node ralph/journal.mjs stub 3.21` before implementing; each attempt appends its own journal line (lesson [1.29]).
acceptance: `scripts/check` green; in the container on the embedded leg (`ESSAYDOWN_E2E_DRIVER=embedded`), before the fix, one-workflow.spec.ts and rewrite.spec.ts fail with the gate's first errors ('producing under heading 1 never matched'; 'Cmd/Ctrl+Enter never added If anything they sharpened it.'), quoted in the journal; after it, every spec file under e2e/shell/test/ passes on both legs, each leg's per-file passing/failing lines recorded in the journal; routes.spec.ts carries guards (a)–(c), the journal naming the test that discharges each and quoting each mutation's result (the route reverted, the spec red, then restored, `git diff` confirmed back; (c)'s recorded as container-green with the reason); `grep -n 'textContent' e2e/shell/test/one-workflow.spec.ts e2e/shell/test/rewrite.spec.ts e2e/shell/test/reorder.spec.ts` shows no offset or length read of an editor block (every remaining hit named in the journal as a non-offset read); `grep -rn 'process.platform' e2e/shell/test/` and `grep -rn '\.skip(' e2e/shell/test/` print nothing; the backlog line and the lessons line appended; `git diff --name-only "$(git merge-base HEAD phase/3)" HEAD` lists only the scope files; no manifest or lockfile change; zero new dependencies (PRD §4); the journal states that (c) is proved only by the macOS e2e-shell leg of the 3.verify.g1h gate and (a)/(b) by the container's embedded leg and both CI legs.

description: Phase 3 review fix, a permutation reanchors stale sidecar positions (DECISIONS #review-3-r0 S2 — Sol r0 finding 2 blocker; taken under Michael's stop rule DECISIONS #041 D1 and his approval of the r0 list (DECISIONS #review-3-r0); files of passed tasks 3.2 and 3.5, whose records are not edited — a new task per DECISIONS #016). Scope: packages/core/src/sidecar.ts, packages/core/test/sidecar.test.ts, packages/core/test/outline.test.ts, packages/core/test/reorder-goldens.test.ts only if a golden's sidecar changes (it must not), docs/lessons.md, the journal. Defect: attach a variant to `Beta here.` in `Alpha here. Beta here.`, type `New first.` before them, then reorder sentences `[0,2,1]` — before the move the panel shows the variant on Beta, after it the stored anchor names Alpha (hash and text rebuilt for the wrong sentence), and a save and reload keep it there; inserting an introductory paragraph and then moving Beta's paragraph before Alpha's does the same through `applyMoveBlock`, and a heading inserted above a section does it to that section's heading question through `applyOutlineDrop`/`applyMoveSection` (Sol's probes, .evidence/reviews/3/r0/sol/core-probes.log:1–33). Cause: `reanchor` (sidecar.ts:531) states "Callers pass a sidecar whose positions are current", and `applyReorderSentences` (:582) and `carryTopLevelMove` (:631) pass `state.sidecar` unchanged; the editor's commit (packages/editor store `commit(root, document.sidecar, …)`) never refreshes positions, so after typing that shifts indices `anchor.pos` names another item. Fix: resolve every entry against the pre-move root before the permutation — pass `refresh(state.sidecar, state.root, options)` (sidecar.ts:504) to `reanchor` in both callers, or make `reanchor` refresh first and drop the caller contract from its doc comment; an entry that does not resolve stays an orphan, never silently moved. Guards, one vitest test each: (1) sentence reorder after a sentence typed before the variant's paragraph keeps the variant on its own text (Sol's probe 1); (2) `applyMoveBlock` after an inserted paragraph (probe 2); (3) `applyMoveSection` / `applyOutlineDrop` after a heading inserted above keeps each heading question on its heading; (4) an entry whose sentence was deleted before the move is an orphan after it (absence case); (5) duplicate sentence text in two paragraphs, one with a variant, the move keeps it on the right one; (6) after each move, the stored hash and text equal `attach`'s for the intended item on the reloaded document; (7) corpus identity leg: for every fixture in fixtures/markdown/index.json, a sidecar whose positions are stale by one inserted paragraph, the identity permutation re-serialises the Markdown byte-identically and the sidecar equals the refreshed one. Record the mutation of the fix (revert one caller) red then restored. Run the suite as `scripts/check`; a long command (an e2e spec) runs as one foreground call bounded by `timeout 540` with its output redirected to a file, never `run_in_background` (DECISIONS #049). Zero new dependencies (PRD §4).
acceptance: packages/core/test holds the seven named guards (titles in the journal) and they are green; the mutation of one caller recorded red then restored (`git diff` confirmed back); the journal names the test that discharges each guard, enumerated from the diff; `git diff --stat` against the branch base touches only the scope files; no manifest or lockfile change; zero new dependencies (PRD §4); `scripts/check` green.

description: Phase 3 review fix, inline code swallows a hard break and a link on save (DECISIONS #review-3-r0 C1, C6 — Claude r0 finding 1 blocker and finding 6 should-fix Required, taken as blocking under D1; the backlog lines `[3.16, found outside scope]` and `[3.12, found outside scope]`, whose hard stop 3.verify recorded as untaken; taken under Michael's stop rule DECISIONS #041 D1 and his approval of the r0 list (DECISIONS #review-3-r0); files of passed tasks 3.12 and 3.16, whose records are not edited — DECISIONS #016). Scope: packages/editor/src/input.ts, packages/editor/src/schema.ts, packages/editor/test/input.test.ts, packages/editor/test/typed-marks.test.ts, one new packages/editor/test file for the hard-break and link-wrapped-code guards, docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md (one line closing the two outside-scope lines), docs/lessons.md, the journal. Defects: (C1) Shift+Enter right after an inline-code run — ```alpha`beta`` with the caret after `alpha` — inserts a `hard_break` carrying `inline_code` (input.ts:226, `replaceSelectionWith`'s default `inheritMarks: true`), and `pmToMdast` folds it into the code run as its empty `textContent` (schema.ts:1409–1416), so the saved file has no break; with a space after the span (```alpha` beta``) the space goes too. (C6) one character typed at the start of a link whose text is a code span — ``[`cd`](v) tail`` — saves ```Xcd` tail``: `runEnd` (schema.ts:1365) extends an `inline_code` run while the mark is in the next node's set, not while the whole mark set is equal, so the typed `code` node and the `code+link` node become one `inlineCode` and the link is never wrapped; at the end it saves ``[`cd`](v)`X```. Before touching the editor's tree, read the installed mdast-util-to-markdown `break` and `inlineCode` handlers and the app's handler for each mark (CLAUDE.md: both halves of every fixed-point family are owned). Fix, by behaviour: a hard break inserted by Shift+Enter never carries `inline_code` and keeps the other marks it inherits today (emphasis, strong, delete, link — DECISIONS #review-1-r8 N1); `pmToMdast` never drops a `hard_break` that does carry `inline_code` (a pasted or hand-built tree), splitting the code run at it; an `inline_code` run is grouped only across nodes whose full mark sets agree, so a `link` boundary is never crossed. A ProseMirror `NodeSpec.marks` on `hard_break` does not restrict the marks on the break itself (it governs content), so the fix is in the command and the converter. Guards, one test each: (1) Shift+Enter at the closing edge and the opening edge of each of the five mark kinds (emphasis, strong, delete, link, inline_code), × the following text spaced / unspaced / block end, with one astral member: the break is present in `format(pmToMdast(·))` and the result is a fixed point of parse∘format; (2) the inserted break's marks equal today's minus `inline_code` (presence of the other four, absence of `inline_code`); (3) a hand-built paragraph whose `hard_break` carries `inline_code` serialises with the break; (4) one character typed at the start and at the end of ``[`cd`](v)``, with and without an enclosing emphasis: the link is present and the node count after `parse(format(·))` equals the tree's (DECISIONS #review-1-r7 M2); (5) a corpus leg seeded from the writing surface: every link-wrapped code span of every fixture in fixtures/markdown/index.json, one character typed at each edge, the output a fixed point and the link count unchanged; (6) the ordered-pair sweep of task 1.67 extended with `inline_code+link` as a composite first run. Remove the `unrepresentable` bound for the `link | O9 | the click route` cells in typed-marks.test.ts only if the fix makes them representable, and say which in the journal. Run the suite as `scripts/check`; a long command (an e2e spec) runs as one foreground call bounded by `timeout 540` with its output redirected to a file, never `run_in_background` (DECISIONS #049). Zero new dependencies (PRD §4).

description: Phase 3 review fix, the save path's notion of dirty and saved (DECISIONS #review-3-r0 S1, S3 — Sol r0 findings 1 and 3, both blocker; taken under Michael's stop rule DECISIONS #041 D1 and his approval of the r0 list (DECISIONS #review-3-r0); files of passed tasks 2.16, 3.2 and 3.19, whose records are not edited — DECISIONS #016). Scope: apps/desktop/src/workspace/document-sync.ts, apps/desktop/src/workspace/DocumentPane.tsx, tests/document-sync.test.ts, tests/sidecar-sync.test.ts, one e2e/shell/test spec case only if a vitest through the pane cannot reach a guard (say which in the journal), docs/lessons.md, the journal. Defects: (S1) open `Alpha.`, toggle to the source view, type `LOCAL`, and let another writer append to the file inside the source coalescing window: after the watcher's 100 ms debounce the buffer and the store hold only the external text, no banner shows, and `LOCAL` is gone (Sol's probe, .evidence/reviews/3/r0/sol/browser-probes.log:1–15). Cause: `check()` (document-sync.ts:288–300) decides on `dirty`, which only a store commit sets (`edited()` from DocumentPane's store subscriber); the pending CodeMirror burst has not committed, so `disk !== known && !dirty` → `reloaded` → the pane rebuilds the store, and the old binding's `destroy()` flushes `LOCAL` into the discarded store — the watcher is a store reader that does not settle (CLAUDE.md). (S3) with an externally malformed sidecar (`{broken`) and one variant added in the app, `flush()` returns `saved`: DocumentPane.tsx:249 reports the parse error and returns normally on `choice.action === "skip"`, so `write()` clears `dirty` and every caller that discards state (switch, close, rename) proceeds and drops the variant (browser-probes.log:16–23; CLAUDE.md, DECISIONS #review-2-r0 U1). Fix: (1) the sync gains a settle step that `check()` runs before its clean/dirty decision, and again after its awaited disk read, and that `keepMine()` runs before it serialises; DocumentPane wires it to the store's `settle()` (the commit fires `edited()` synchronously, so the decision sees `dirty`). (2) The sidecar skip branch fails through the existing MarkdownWritten path — the Markdown baseline stays the written one, the document stays dirty, `flush()` resolves `failed`, and the error names the sidecar as not saved; no new dialog or button (Michael's answer: the escape hatch is backlog). Guards, one test each (vitest with fake timers through the pane and mocked invoke/listen, the shape the existing switch and toggle tests use): (1) an external change inside the source window after typing → the banner, the buffer and the store keep `LOCAL`; (2) the same change arriving during the watcher's awaited read (DECISIONS #review-2-r2 W1 shape) → the same; (3) Keep mine inside the window → disk holds the pending text; (4) no pending burst → reload as today (absence case); (5) malformed disk sidecar plus an in-memory variant → `flush()` is `failed`, the Markdown is written, the variant retained; (6) switch, close and rename each stay on the document on that `failed` (one test per caller); (7) after the sidecar is repaired on disk, the next save writes it and the variant survives a reload; (8) a well-formed sidecar → `saved` (absence case). Record the mutation of each fix red then restored. Run the suite as `scripts/check`; a long command (an e2e spec) runs as one foreground call bounded by `timeout 540` with its output redirected to a file, never `run_in_background` (DECISIONS #049). Zero new dependencies (PRD §4).
